links.description: Offers online selection of classic stories for kids and teens. Includes links to short stories for kids.

links.title: Young People's Zone
links.description: A site with children's literature online sorted by series and author.  Includes fairy tales, Avonlea series, fables, Robin Hood tales, and other classics

links.title: The War of the Worlds
links.description: E-text of The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells.

links.title: The Online Books Page
links.description: Electronic texts archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.  Search or browse by author/title/subject.

links.title: Jack London's Writings
links.description: A collection of electronic text versions of novels and short stories by Jack London.

links.title: Lynch Multimedia
links.description: Includes Shakespeare's plays with audio, and the original.

links.title: From Mother Goose in Prose by Frank Baum
links.description: Includes story versions of a few rhymes.

links.title: Electronic Texts Formated by Robert Stockton
links.description: A collection of over twenty electronic text versions of classics reformatted for easy reading.

links.title: World of Tales
links.description: A collection of classic stories for children, including folktales, fairy tales and fables.

451206.title: Aesop's Fables
451206.description: A fable is a short story or poem that teaches a lesson or moral. Aesop's fables date back to 6th century B.C.

links.title: Fables of Aesop
links.description: Compilation of nearly 400 fables from several existing translations. Includes a list of the animals that are used as primary characters in the fables, and links to the fables in which they appear.

links.title: Proverbs from Aesop's Fables
links.description: Titles of fables and their proverbs.

links.title: Aesop's Fables
links.description: Features short tales that were written or recorded by the ancient Greek citizen, Aesop. Some stories on the site are static and others are animated with sound. Page includes biography.

links.title: Aesop's Fables - Online Collection
links.description: A collection of Aesop's and other fables. There are more than 655 fables indexed with Morals, Fairy Tales, Mythology, and Stories.

links.title: Aesop's Phrases
links.description: A table listing some phrases we use in everyday speech and the fables from which these phrases have come.

451208.title: Alcott, Louisa May
451208.description: This category lists pages and sites that discuss the works of American author Louisa May Alcott (1832-1888), or provide complete online texts. Alcott is best remembered for her classic novel Little Women.

links.title: Bibliomania: Louisa M. Alcott
links.description: Provides complete texts of An Old Fashioned Girl, Eight Cousins, Good Wives, and Little Women and provides an introduction to Alcott's writings.

links.title: UPenn Digital Library:  Little Men
links.description: Complete text.

links.title: Louisa May Alcott Electronic Text from University of Pennsylvania
links.description: Electronic text catalog for the works of Louisa May Alcott archived by the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

links.title: Eight Cousins by Louisa May Alcott
links.description: Read about Rosie Campbell, who becomes an orphan after her father's death and is sent to live with her six aunts and seven cousins (all boys).

451197.title: Andersen, Hans Christian
451197.description: This category lists pages and sites that provide texts discuss the works of Danish Author Hans Christian Andersen (1805-1875). Andersen's fairy tales have delighted generations of children.

links.title: Hans Christian Andersen: Fairy Tales and Stories
links.description: English translation includes original illustrations by Vilhelm Pedersen and Lorenz Frølich. Includes texts of more than 100 of Andersen's tales.

links.title: Works of Hans Christian Andersen
links.description: Electronic text for the works of Hans Christian Andersen archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

links.title: Fairy Tales of Hans Christian Andersen
links.description: Text of 127 fairy tales.

451209.title: Baum, L. Frank
451209.description: This category lists pages and sites that provide online texts or discuss the works of L. Frank Baum (1856-1919). Baum is best known as creator of the Wizard of Oz.

links.title: Electronic Text - Works of L. Frank Baum
links.description: Electronic text for the works of L. Frank Baum archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

links.title: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
links.description: Complete text of the Christmas novel, broken into chapters.

links.title: Online Literature Library: L Frank Baum
links.description: Provides complete online texts for all of Baum's 14 novels about the world of Oz.

451204.title: Brothers Grimm
451204.description: Jacob Grimm (1785-1863) and Wilhelm Grimm (1786-1859), linguists, became famous for their collection of folktales, "Grimm's Fairy Tales". Jacob Grimm also wrote "German Mythology". This category is for e-texts and sites about their works.

links.title: Animated Grimm Fairy Tales
links.description: Read, listen, and look at the Grimm Brother's Fairy Tales in these fully animated versions. [Flash required]

links.title: Grimm's Fairy Tales
links.description: Sound recordings of popular stories can be played online or downloaded as a music file. Each one is given a new twist by the actors.

451199.title: Carroll, Lewis
451199.description:
This category lists pages and sites that discuss the works of British author Charles Lutwidge Dodgson (1832-1898) or provide free online texts.

Dodgson wrote under the pen name Lewis Carroll. Also a brilliant mathematician and logician, he is best remembered for giving the world Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

links.title: Bibliomania: Lewis Carroll
links.description: An introduction to Carroll's writings, summaries of his most popular works, and online texts.

links.title: Alice in Wonderland
links.description: A read-aloud version of the classic story complete with illustrations from John Tenniel and 10 other artists.

links.title: Lewis Carroll Electronic Texts
links.description: Electronic text for the works of Lewis Carroll archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

links.title: Adventures In Wonderland
links.description: Recounts the tale of the girl who falls asleep and has a most peculiar dream of falling down a hole into a world she has never seen.

links.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
links.description: Complete text with the original Tenniel illustrations available.

links.title: Alice's Adventures Under Ground
links.description: A shorter version of the original Alice tales.

links.title: Online Literature Library: Lewis Carroll
links.description: Archive of Carroll's more well-known writings, including Alice in Wonderland and "The Hunting of the Snark."

451202.title: Collodi, Carlo
451202.description: Carlo Collodi is the pen name of Italian author Carlo Lorenzini. His most famous book is Pinocchio. His mother was born in a village called Collodi and he chose that for his pen name.

links.title: The Literature Page: The Adventures of Pinocchio by Carlo Collodi
links.description: Translated by Carol Della Chiesa. Text in html format for online reading. Readers may place up to 10 books on a "bookshelf" which uses cookies to mark the last page read.

links.title: Pinocchio
links.description: Online presentation of the book by C. Collodi; illustrated by Frederick Richardson; published by The John C. Winston Co., 1927.

451200.title: Dickens, Charles
451200.description: Dickens was a British author in the 1800's. This category is for his works. It's scope includes e-texts and commentary.

451207.title: Kipling, Rudyard
451207.description: In 1907 he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, the first and youngest English winner of this award. This category is for his works. It will contain e-texts and commentary.

links.title: Complete Collection of Poems by Rudyard Kipling
links.description: Includes well-known texts such as Gunga Din and Mandalay. With a brief biography.

451198.title: Montgomery, Lucy Maud
451198.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about the works of Canadian author Lucy Maud Montgomery (1874-1942) or provide free online versions of them. Montgomery gave the world such timeless heroines as Anne of Green Gables and Emily of New Moon.

links.title: Lucy Maude Montgomery Electronic Texts
links.description: Electronic texts for the works of L. M. Montgomery archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

451210.title: Shakespeare, William
451210.description: This category lists pages and sites about the works of British playwright and poet William Shakespeare (1564-1616). It includes links to online texts, plot summaries study notes, and related quizzes and activities.

links.title: Bartleby: Shakespeare
links.description: Provides complete texts of a range of plays and poems. Includes a search feature.

links.title: William Shakespeare Electronic Texts
links.description: Electronic text of the works of William Shakespeare archived by the University of Pennsylvania Digital Archive.

links.title: Surfing with the Bard - Shakespeare High
links.description: Includes information about Shakespeare's plays and poems, fun activities for students, and ideas for teachers.

links.title: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
links.description: Complete html texts of all plays.

451205.title: Shelley, Mary
451205.description: The works of Mary Shelley. This category will include e-texts and commentary.

links.title: Frankenstein, by Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
links.description: HTML text online.

451203.title: Twain, Mark
451203.description: This category lists pages and sites related to the works of American writer and humorist Samuel Langhorne Clemens (1835-1910) who wrote under the pen name Mark Twain. It includes e-texts, plot summaries, study notes, and interactive activities.

links.title: Mark Twain Electronic Texts
links.description: Electronic text of the works of Mark Twain archived at the University of Pennsylvania Digital Library.

links.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
links.description: Complete text of the 1876 work about a boy's adventures along the Mississippi.

links.title: The Literature Page - Mark Twain
links.description: Read some of the most well-known fiction novels and essays written by the Missouri author.

links.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
links.description: Etext and study resources from the University of Virginia.

links.title: Aesop's Fables
links.description: Traditional and modern versions, illustrated and retold by art students at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst. Requires Flash plug-in.

links.title: Myth, Fable and Traditional
links.description: Explains the difference between myths, fables, and legends. Also offers an assortment of each.

links.title: Storytymes' Aesop's Fables
links.description: Aesop's Fables in mp3 format with music and sound effects that help bring the characters to life, download then play to hear the story.

links.title: Folklore and Mythology Electronic Texts
links.description: Vast collection of folktales, myths, legends, and texts pertaining to folklore, arranged by title and theme, with a focus on northern and western Europe.

links.title: The Encyclopedia Mythica
links.description: An online encyclopedia of mythology, folklore, and legend from different cultures and religions all over the world.

links.title: World Myths and Legends in Art
links.description: Learn about myths of different cultures.  Look up by theme or region of influence.  Includes photographs of artwork that were used to portray these ideas.  Presented by the Minneapolis Institute of Arts.

links.title: Bulfinch's Mythology
links.description: Access to Roman mythology information including Pandora, Hercules, and Orion.

links.title: The Fairy Chronicles
links.description: Modern fairy tales with magical creatures such as fairies, trolls, and wizards.

451212.title: King Arthur
451212.description: This categories lists sites about King Arthur, the legendary ruler of the Britons said to have brought peace to the country and established a kingdom based on law and justice.

links.title: Merrie Haskell's King Arthur
links.description: Examines the legends of King Arthur in their historical and political context.

links.title: King Arthur
links.description: The village of Caerleon, fabled to be the location of King Arthur's Camelot, explores a few of the legends associated with him.

451213.title: Robin Hood
451213.description: This category lists pages and sites about Robin Hood, the legendary hero of medieval England said to have stolen from the rich and given to the poor.

links.title: Robin Hood
links.description: Includes historical articles, ballads, pictures, and a guide to the tales of England's most famous outlaw and his merry band of robbers. Also provides a glimpse into the live of the real characters who inspired the tales.

links.title: Who killed Cock Robin?
links.description: Read the nursery rhyme with its history and origins which allude to the legend of Robin Hood.

links.title: Legends: The Robin Hood Pages
links.description: Features a short introduction and a guide to resources on the net.

links.title: The Academy of American Poets
links.description: Searchable index of poems and poet biographies. Also includes audio files of works read by the author.

links.title: Poetry for Kids
links.description: Features poetry for kids about animals, weather, and aliens.

links.title: FizzyFunnyFuzzy.com
links.description: Humorous, entertaining and fun poetry for children.

links.title: ShelSilverstein.com
links.description: Features animations, information about the author, activities for young readers, e-cards, and resources for teachers and parents.

links.title: Kristine O'Connell George
links.description: Features author information, ideas for students, audio clips, and poetry quotes.

links.title: Funny Poems For Kids
links.description: Includes funny poems, riddles, jokes, and tongue twisters.

links.title: Poets'  Corner
links.description: Features a collection of works gathered from many different sources. Contains indexes of authors, titles and subjects, biographies, illustrations, and FAQs.

links.title: A Dictionary of Haiku
links.description: Contains a list of haiku poems.

links.title: Poetry 180
links.description: A poem a day provided by the Library of Congress, one for each of the 180 days of a typical American high school year.

links.title: Funny Rhymes
links.description: Weblog with a collection of original nursery rhymes.

links.title: Mama Lisa's World
links.description: An archive of nursery rhymes and children's songs from all over the world.

links.title: Writebuzz
links.description: A fully moderated site, featuring poetry and short stories; with new writing competitions on a regular basis.

links.title: River of Words
links.description: Poetry and art by children from around the world about the natural world. Free annual contest in affiliation with Library of Congress.

links.title: The Poetry Zone
links.description: Features poems and book reviews written by kids, interviews with poets and a teacher zone. Includes videos.

links.title: Mother Goose Illustrated
links.description: Complete collection of Mother Goose nursery rhymes with contemporary illustrations. Rhymes are searchable and categorized.

links.title: Imaginesongs
links.description: A collection of original poems, songs, skits and animations by children's author and playwright Joe Thompson.

links.title: Children's Poetry Archive
links.description: Collection of poems written by and for children. It also has competitions for young poets ready for a challenge.

links.title: Teen Ink: Poetry
links.description: Large collection of poems by teens from the archives of this online and print magazine.

451189.title: Series
451189.description: This category lists pages and sites about popular series novels for children and young adults.

links.title: Trailblazer Books
links.description: Introduces the action-packed historical fiction series by  Dave and Neta Jackson which introduces young people to Christian heroes. Includes downloadable short stories and a look at new titles.

links.title: The Official Berenstain Bears Website
links.description: Includes book-related activities, video clips, and listing of all books. Also allows children to send e-mail to the Berenstain Bears and receive a reply.

links.title: Dr. Seuss's Seussville
links.description: Includes interactive games, contests, and information on Seuss and his works.

links.title: Goosebumps
links.description: Scholastic's site for the popular book and TV series. Each of the goblins and ghouls from the series host their own scary section.

links.title: Little House
links.description: Official site introduces Laura's family and helps readers learn more about their own heritage. Also includes complete listing of books and introduction to the many generations of Little House authors.

links.title: Little Critter
links.description: Jokes, puzzles, games and stories from children author and illustrator, Mercer Mayer.

links.title: Dear America
links.description: Official site tells about the books and television series inspired by the diaries and letters from girls who lived in different periods in American history. Site includes book excerpts, craft ideas, historical postcards, and contests.

links.title: Captain Underpants
links.description: Official site tells about the pint-size heroes of this series and offers fun activities and games related to the books. Also includes guide for grown-ups.

links.title: Paolini.net
links.description: Official site. Offers updates on the Inheritance trilogy, by Christopher Paolini. Includes notes from the author, information about the land Alagaesia, and free newsletter.

links.title: Paddington Bear
links.description: Official site tells about the loveable bear, his books, and his TV show. Also includes game, puzzle, coloring page, downloadable screensaver and e-cards.

links.title: The Black Stallion
links.description: Official site provides information about Black Stallion books and movie. Includes biographical sketch of series author Walter Farley and sneak previews of upcoming books.

links.title: Magic Tree House
links.description: Official site tells about each book in this fictional series that takes readers around the world. Also features the authors' scrapbook, their answers to common questions, and a readers and writers' club.

links.title: Junie B. Jones
links.description: Official site introduces the character and the books in her series. Also includes printable coloring pages and activity sheets as well as a visit with the author.

451190.title: Hardy Boys, The
451190.description: This category contains sites related to The Hardy Boys series of books and their creators, authors, and publishers.

links.title: Hardy Boys Encyclopedia
links.description: Find cover scans, character appearances, locations guide, forums, book summaries, and site updates.

links.title: The Hardy Boys Unofficial Online Resource
links.description: Features character profiles, articles, series history, reference books, title checklist, polls, a FAQ, and a record of Frank and Joe's travels.

451193.title: Harry Potter
451193.description:
J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter series is intended to comprise seven books. Five have been published so far. They are:

  1. Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (known as Harry Potter and the Sorceror's Stone in the USA)
  2. Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
  3. Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
  4. Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
  5. Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix

links.title: Mugglenet
links.description: Features interactive forums, Potter profiles, and information about the books and the movie.

links.title: Harry Potter
links.description: Official site of the Warner Bros. production. Includes virtual Hogwarts, diversions, online community, news and events, and other magical activities.

links.title: Scholastic Books: Harry Potter
links.description: From Scholastic, the US publisher. Discussion guides for all four books, sample chapters for the first three, an interview with Rowling, excerpts from reviews, games, and a screensaver for both Mac and Windows users. [Requires Flash]

451194.title: Fan Pages
451194.description: This category is for sites made by fans of the Harry Potter books.

links.title: Crazy For Harry Potter
links.description: Facts and rumors about the books, fan fiction, fan club, theories, humor, and encyclopedia of details.

links.title: The Great Hall
links.description: Fan site with news, forums, lessons, interviews of J.K. Rowling, and book reviews.

links.title: The Semi-Intellectual Harry Potter Shrine
links.description: Fan fiction, name games, theories, news, and a distorting mirror gallery of possible Harry characters.

links.title: Harry Potter's Realm of Wizardry
links.description: Contains quotes from the books, character biographies, fan fiction, artwork, news, and a chat room.

links.title: Hearts of Fire
links.description: Contains images, fanart, news, and actor biographies.

links.title: Hogsmeade
links.description: Find forums and gallery. Includes registration information.

451192.title: Nancy Drew
451192.description: This category contains sites related to the Nancy Drew series of books and their creators, authors, and publishers.

links.title: Nancy Drew Sleuth
links.description: Designed for fans and collectors of Nancy Drew. Provides information on this plucky sleuth including history, books, formats and pictures.

links.title: Beyond Nancy Drew
links.description: An annotated bibliography of books for girls written in the last two hundred years which reflect the roles for girls considered proper at the time.

451191.title: Series of Unfortunate Events, A
451191.description: Lemony Snicket aka Daniel Handler has written a series of Unfortunate Events about the Baudelaire family.

links.title: The Unauthorized Lemony Snicket FAQ
links.description: Provides information about the characters, contest, abbreviations, interviews, VFD, the family tree, theories, and news updates.

links.title: Fandom: A Wiki of Unfortunate Events
links.description: A Wikipedia-like site all about A Series of Unfortuate Events and Lemony Snicket's world.

451195.title: Sweet Valley
451195.description: Sweet Valley books and books based on the characters of the Sweet Valley books. (Includes Elizabeth, Sweet Valley Kids, Sweet Valley Twins, Sweet Valley Junior High, Sweet Valley High, Sweet Valley High Senior Year, and Sweet Valley University.)

links.title: Sweet Valley
links.description: Official site gives the scoop on everything that's going on in Sweet Valley. Also includes about the author.

links.title: SVUnited
links.description: Reviews of Sweet Valley books with accompanying cover pictures.

451180.title: Reading
451180.description: This category contains sites that provide information, tips, guides, and activities to help kids and teens learn to read or improve their reading skills.

links.title: Book Adventure
links.description: A free on-line reading program encourages students in grades K-8 to read more often, for longer periods of time, and with greater understanding. Requires free registration.

links.title: Read Today: A Language Reading Platform
links.description: Interactive site helps young students learn letters of the alphabet and other basic literacy skills.

links.title: World Book Day
links.description: Official site of the yearly event. Introduces the day, lists events, and lists book recommendations.  Also pictures of past events.

links.title: Starfall
links.description: Free site to teach the basics of reading. Features interactive books and phonics games.

links.title: Nursery Rhymes Lyrics and Origins
links.description: Nursery rhymes with their history and origins.

links.title: Sight Words Exercises
links.description: Contains online words games.

links.title: dreambeast poems
links.description: Poems and stories to inspire children to laugh, think, explore, and believe.

links.title: Book a Prize
links.description: Encourages children and young adults to enrich reading skills and with the guidance of parents, get prizes for achievements.

links.title: Reading Is Fundamental’s Literacy Central
links.description: Digital library hosts over 10,000 resources directly tied to the books. Helps to organize all book resources in one place, create and share book lists, find helpful reading tips and strategies and track reading progress.

451181.title: Alphabet Fun
451181.description: This category contains sites that are specifically for learning the letters of the alphabet and associating them with words that begin with the letters.

links.title: Jan Brett Alphabet
links.description: Printable alphabet flash cards in traditional manuscript, cursive, and modern manuscript.

links.title: Animal Alphabet
links.description: Animated page includes animal and short rhyme for each letter of the alphabet

links.title: EnchantedLearning.com: Picture Dictionary with Links
links.description: Click on the letter of the alphabet at the top and see words and pictures that begin with that letter.

links.title: Alphabet Fun from PrimaryGames.com
links.description: Includes games, e-book, and printable coloring and activity pages.

links.title: Create-a-Reader
links.description: Find small and capital letters and listen to their sounds.

links.title: Alphabetimals
links.description: Animated cartoon characters combine animals shapes with letter shapes and sounds to make it fun for kids learn and remember their ABCs.

links.title: Ms. Bernett's Kindergarten Class
links.description: Webquest teaching students all about the alphabet. Topics include; alphabet song, order of letters, matching uppercase to lowercase letters. It includes informational websites, and alphabet games for the students.

451182.title: Book Reviews
451182.description: This category contains sites which provide book reviews for kids and teens.

links.title: Spaghetti Book Club
links.description: Collection of children's book reviews written and illustrated by kids for kids. Read posted reviews or submit new ones.

links.title: Read Up On It
links.description: Book reviews from the National Library of Canada. Includes  age level recommendations and groups the books by subject.

links.title: A Young Reader's Opinion
links.description: This is a site for those looking to comment and debate about come commonly read teen books.

links.title: Reader Views Kids
links.description: Book reviews by kids for kids.

links.title: My Weekly Bookshelf
links.description: Created by two teenage girls with a passion for books. Avid readers, they post reviews, author info, pics, new book release information.  Includes their personal work in the field of literature and poetry.

links.title: Libraries and Young Adults
links.description: Youth services librarian reviews books for teens and lets them know about programs offered in libraries.

links.title: Book Heaven
links.description: Teen and Young Adult book news, author news and book reviews.

links.title: The Book Club Girls
links.description: Book reviews, recommendations, and calendars for new books.  For girls ages 12-16.

links.title: YALSA Book Awards and Booklists
links.description: Recommended reading for teens ages 12 - 18 as selected by the Young Adult Library Services Association (YALSA).

links.title: susanthelibrarian
links.description: Storyteller and youth services librarian gives reviews of fiction and nonfiction books for kids and teens.

451168.title: Speaking
451168.description:
This category contains information, tips, guides, and activities to help kids and teens with assignments in public speaking, writing speeches, and debating.

It is not about speech therapy nor about the political aspects of speech, e.g. the First Amendment.

links.title: Preparing Speeches
links.description: Offers ten-steps for preparing and delivering a speech. Includes selecting a topic, researching, outlining, using visual aids, and practicing.

links.title: The History Place: Great Speeches Collection
links.description: Read some of the most famous speeches ever delivered. Listed in alphabetical order by speaker.

links.title: Tongue Twister Database for English Language Learners
links.description: Dozens of tongue twisters sorted by primary letter sound.

451214.title: Style
451214.description:
This category contains sites that provide information, tips, guides, and activities to help kids and teens learn proper composition style and usage.

Style includes learning how to avoid the use of cliches, slang, and overly complicated or long-winded methods of conveying meaning in writing.

links.title: Plain English Campaign
links.description: Working internationally to try to get public information written in plain English, instead of using gobbledygook, jargon and legalese. Includes examples, with annual awards for the worst offenders.

links.title: Cliche Finder
links.description: A searchable database of overused expressions, with a fun feature creating a random list.

links.title: The Sports Cliche List
links.description: A searchable collection of cliches used by American teams, fans, coaches and commentators, with humorous comments and sound clips.

links.title: Plain Language
links.description: A guide to help writers avoid confusing language and long-windedness. Can be viewed online or downloaded as a PDF.

links.title: Capitalizing
links.description: Provides a list of rules and examples. Includes sentences, quotations, proper nouns, names, titles, and scientific nomenclature.

links.title: The Elements of Style - William Strunk
links.description: Principal requirements of plain English style. Focuses on the rules of usage in literature, composition and grammar.

links.title: Guide to Grammar and Writing
links.description: Features searchable index of grammatical rules, explanations, comments on style, and usage suggestions.

links.title: Grammar Slammer
links.description: This help file indexes style and usage, capitalization, abbreviations, punctuation, letter writing, common mistakes and a grammar glossary.

links.title: Literary Devices
links.description: A resource for students learning the various literary devices used in the English language.

451184.title: Vocabulary
451184.description:
This category contains sites that provide educational tips, guides, and activities to help kids improve their vocabulary.

Sites might include vocabulary games, word puzzles, explanations of prefixes and suffixes, derivatives, or origins.

links.title: What's the Word
links.description: Online game to learn reading and expand vocabulary. From Funbrain.com.

links.title: Learning Vocabulary Can Be Fun
links.description: Hangman, matching, word search, and vocabulary trivia to help students learn vocabulary.

links.title: Word Traps
links.description: Provides an alphabetical list of words which are often misused. Includes definition and corrected usage.

links.title: iVocabulary.com
links.description: Offers tests to build students' vocabularies, as practice for the SAT, or for ESL students. Difficulty increases with each correct answer.

links.title: Dolch Word List
links.description: A flash-card type vocabulary list of 220 common words.

links.title: SAT Vocabulary Tests on Vocab Test.com
links.description: A series of interactive tests designed to help students learn standard SAT words.

451185.title: Slang
451185.description: A kind of language used instead of normal words. Often used for humor or to identify the speaker as part of a group.

links.title: Commonly-Used American Slang
links.description: An alphabetical list of words and expressions, set out as a quiz with hidden answers.

links.title: Twists, Slugs and Roscoes: A Glossary of Hardboiled Slang
links.description: Definitions of the lingo used in the crime fiction and movies of the '30's and '40's.

451169.title: Writing
451169.description:
This category contains sites which provide information, tips, guides, and activities to help kids and teens improve writing skills.

Topics include essays and reports, poetry, punctuation, spelling, and handwriting.

links.title: Fiction Writing Careers
links.description: Learn more about pursuing fiction as a career, with insights on the publishing industry, making a living as a professional author, and the craft of writing books, stories, and screenplays.

links.title: Paragraph Builder
links.description: Step-by-step directions for organizing and writing a good paragraph.

links.title: paragraphpunch.com
links.description: An online writing tutorial; takes students through the actual steps of writing a paragraph online.

links.title: ABC's of the Writing Process
links.description: Tips for each of the five stages of the writing process.

links.title: Myths, Folktales and Fairy Tales
links.description: Resource for learning about and writing in these genres.

links.title: Science Fiction Writing Activity
links.description: Use nonfiction science to create a science fiction story.

links.title: Swords of Writing

451179.title: Turabian-Chicago Format

Check with the instructor who assigned your paper to determine whether you need to use notes or whether you can cite sources parenthetically in your text.

451155.title: Korean

This category lists sites that help English-speaking children and teens learn the Korean language.

The phonetic alphabet consists of eleven vowels and fourteen consonants, which represent every sound in the Korean language. Even today it is considered to be one of the most efficient alphabets in the world.

Korean is read from left to right and from the top of the page to the bottom.

451845.title: Counting and Numbers
451845.description:
Counting is the method of naming "whole" numbers, in order, from a smaller number to a larger one. It is an essential part of math to be able to know the number names and understand what they mean, similar to reciting the letters of the alphabet.

Numbers have four ways of being represented. For example the number 3 can be recognised as

  • a) 3
  • b) three
  • c) III
  • d) speaking the word "three"

451827.title: History
451827.description:
Mathematics has been around since the development of written language and probably before that. The field of working with numbers and formulas first came from practical uses such as counting crops, measuring land, astronomical data for sailing, and trading in the market square.

The field of math, in its many forms, has developed in all parts of the world from the Mayans to the Mexican region to Africa and Europe and China. As more texts are found and translated, it will be very exciting to see what we will find.

Important developments in math includes counting, writing of numbers, calculating amounts, working with fractions, creating a number system, using variables, using graphs and applying these ideas to the real world.

451227.title: Science
451227.description:
Sites and resources for children and teens under the age of 18 dealing with general scientific topics.

Science can be defined as a process of recording data from controlled experiments, summarizing the results and then attempting to develop a rational theory to describe these results. Not all experiments lead to a successful theory, but yield results that cannot be summed up in a useful way.

Science fields include biology, chemistry, physics, astronomy, earth sciences, environmental studies, and technology.

Math is closely related to science and is a necessary component of most sciences. Most branches of math do not conduct experiments, so that is why it is listed in a separate section.

The applications of successful scientific theories and applications can be astonishing. Without science, there would be no detailed environmental knowledge, electricity, space travel, air conditioning, cars, or washing machines.

There are also, some negative affects from science, such as the development of nuclear weapons and non-biodegradable plastics.

We, as a society, have choices to make on how to use these scientific developments.

451676.description: Hydrogen was recognized as a distinct element by Henry Cavendish in 1776. It is one of the most abundant substances in the Universe.

links.title: Wikipedia: Hydrogen
links.description: Includes an article with pictures covering properties, applications, history, forms and safety precautions.

links.title: ChemicalElements.com: Hydrogen
links.description: Features basic information, an atomic structure diagram, facts and a table of isotopes.

links.title: It's Elemental: Hydrogen
links.description: Includes physical properties and information about the uses and history of hydrogen.

451677.title: Nitrogen
451677.description: Nitrogen was discovered in 1772 by Daniel Rutherford. Nitrogen makes up 78% of the Earth's air. Nitrogen is found in all living systems as a component of biological compounds.

links.title: Wikipedia: Nitrogen
links.description: Article detailing physical properties, history, applications, characteristics and safety precautions.

links.title: ChemicalElements.com: Nitrogen
links.description: Features properties, an atomic structure diagram, facts about nitrogen and a table of isotopes.

451674.title: Oxygen
451674.description: Oxygen was generally thought to be discovered in 1774 by Joseph Priestly, but was also independently identified by Scheele. It is the third most abundant element in the Sun and plays an important role in the carbon-nitrogen cycle in plants.

links.title: Wikipedia: Oxygen
links.description: Article covering properties of the element, including its history, applications, and characteristics as well as safety precautions.

links.title: ChemicalElements.com: Oxygen
links.description: Features basic information, an atomic structure diagram, facts about oxygen and a table of isotopes.

links.title: WebElements: Oxygen
links.description: History, uses, occurrence, compounds, and properties. Features a picture of liquid oxygen and a sound file.

links.title: Visual Elements: Oxygen

451671.title: Games
451671.description: Submit sites that are games that instruct kids/teens on the importance, use, and concepts of chemistry.

links.description: Online and printable games based on the periodic table of elements.

links.title: Periodic Table of the Elements
links.description: Includes combining capacity and online print version.

links.title: Chemicool Periodic Table
links.description: Detailed information on each element.

451793.title: Environment
451793.description: All sites in this category are geared toward kids and teens ages 3-18 and provide information or activities related to nature and environment.

451807.title: Acid Rain
451807.description: Acid rain is caused when certain chemicals are released into the atmosphere, chemically react, and fall as rain or snow. Acid rain has a pH that is much lower than normal rainwater. pH measures if a substance is an acid or a base.

451798.title: Biodiversity
451798.description: Biodiversity refers to the complex relationship between plants, animals, humans, and the environment. If variety in one part is reduced, the other parts are also affected.

links.title: Hinterland Who's Who
links.description: Descriptions of Canadian wildlife, and how you can help preserve it. Includes details of endangered species and habitats, photographs, and movies.

links.title: WWF

links.title: Biodiversity Hotspots
links.description: An interactive world map of the places where plants and animals are most threatened. Includes a searchable database of all land-dwelling vertebrates.

links.title: National Park Service: Kids in Park
links.description: Charged with the trust of preserving the natural resources of America.

451799.title: Deforestation
451799.description: Deforestation is the removal of forested areas, so that they no longer are forests.

links.title: Wikipedia: Deforestation
links.description: Encyclopedia article explains deforestation and how it affects the environment.

links.title: National Geographic: Deforestation

451800.title: Desertification
451800.description: Desertification is the process of land turning into deserts, caused from various factors including climatic variations and human activities.

451796.title: Climate Change

links.title: EIA Energy Kids
links.description: Find out what is energy, its history, sources and conservation tips. With games and activities.

links.title: Geothermal Energy
links.description: Explains how we get geothermal energy with pictures.

links.title: Renewable Energy Facts For Kids
links.description: Facts about renewable energy, power that comes from natural sources that can refill themselves.

links.title: Renewable Energy Sources
links.description: A guide to the sources of renewable energy.

links.description: An illustrated explanation, as well as lists of advantages and disadvantages.

451802.title: Wind

451791.title: Experiments

451347.title: Birds
451347.description: Around 150 million years ago, flying dinosaurs called Pterosaurs began to change (evolve) and develop feathers. This is where scientists believe Birds, as we know them, got their start. Over thousands and thousands of years, there have been thousands and thousands of bird types. Many have become extinct. Others have evolved into one of the 9,000 species of birds that now live on our planet. Birds have learned to live almost everywhere on Earth. From freezing arctic areas to tropical islands and everywhere in between, there are native birds and birds that just come for a visit. Around the world, many of these native birds are endangered. Changes like global warming, pollution, and more humans building more buildings, are destroying the places where they live and feed.

451349.title: Cranes
451349.description:
Cranes are large to very large birds, with long legs and necks, streamlined bodies, and rounded wings. The 15 species live in wetlands and grasslands around the world, except South America. Some migrate; others do not.

The smallest is the Demoiselle Crane; the largest, the Sarus Crane, is the world's tallest flying bird.

Within the crane family are two groups.

  • Crowned Cranes have tawny crests on their heads, prehensile toes that let them roost in trees, and are found only in Africa.
  • Typical Cranes tolerate colder weather, nest on the ground, and can be found around the world.

451382.description: Raptors are meat-eating birds, also called birds of prey, that have keen eyesight, 8 sharp talons, and a hooked beak.  There are more than 450 kinds of raptors. Some birds have learned to live with humans and have their nests on tall buildings in big cities.

451385.title: Eagles
451385.description:
Eagles are medium to large-sized birds of prey that use soaring or sprinting flight to hunt. They build a stick nest and lay 1 - 3 eggs that have a green inner lining. There are four different types of eagles.

Typical or booted eagles range in size and shape from small hawk-eagles to large soaring eagles.

Serpent or snake-eagles mainly eat reptiles and carrion. The lower legs are covered by armor-like scales that help protect against snakebites.

Forest eagles live in tropical rainforests, and include some of the largest and most powerful eagles. Their lower legs are not feathered.

Sea or fish-eagles are large, powerful, long-winged eagles. These eagles do not have feathers on their lower legs. They have rough surfaces on the pads of their feet for holding slippery fish.

links.description: Facts about this national symbol include where it lives, what it eats, how big its nests are, why it was endangered, and how it is being protected.

links.title: Biology of Bald Eagles in Arizona

links.title: Kids' Planet: Bald Eagle

links.title: Bald Eagle Fact Sheet - National Zoo

451387.title: Golden
451387.description:
Golden Eagles get their name from the golden colored feathers on the back of their heads.

Sites in this category have been judged to be of interest to kids and/or teens.

links.title: Golden Eagle

links.title: Golden Eagle

451392.title: Falcons
451392.description:
Falcons are birds of prey (raptors) that are related to hawks and eagles. They have long, pointed wings; a medium to long tail; a short neck; and a short, hooked beak. They can be 6 to 25 inches long and weigh up to 4 pounds.

Species of falcon include kestrels, caracaras, hobbies, falconets, and merlins.

Strong, fast fliers, falcons strike or grab their prey with sharp claws. Most eat birds, reptiles, and small mammals. Some, however, only eat insects or carrion.

Several species of falcons are endangered.

links.description: Learn what they eat, how they hunt, how they pick a mate, where they make their nests, and where they prefer to live. From Texas Parks and Wildlife.

links.title: Northern Aplomado Falcon
links.description: Texas Parks and Wildlife explains their history, habitat, threats and reasons for decline, and what is being done to help their recovery.

links.title: American Peregrine Falcon

links.title: Hobby

links.title: Falcon
links.description: Learn about all the species of falcon, where they live, what they eat, how fast they can fly, and why many are endangered.

links.title: Wingspan: New Zealand Falcon
links.description: Find out why this raptor is threatened, what they sound like, how fast they fly, and where they build their nests.

links.title: Gyrfalcon

links.title: Merlin

links.title: Mauritius Kestrel

451393.title: Caracaras
451393.description:
Caracaras are falcons with a narrow face, a large beak without notches, slit-shaped nostrils, and weak feet with blunt talons. They usually walk while searching for food.

Caracaras live in the Western Hemisphere and are the only falcons to build stick nests.

links.title: Crested Caracara
links.description: The Aviary tells how big this raptor is, what they eat, where they live and how they build their nests.

links.title: Crested Caracara
links.description: The Peregrine Fund explains what this raptor looks like, where it lives, what it eats, and what its name means. See photos and take a quiz.

451389.title: Hawks
451389.description:
Hawks are a group of birds of prey in the family Accipitridae. These birds have slender bodies with short broad rounded wings and a long tail. They have long legs, long sharp talons, and a sharp hooked bill. There are four groups of hawks.

Accipiters or true hawks inhabit forests. They have short, broad, round wings and a long tail; long shins and long, slender toes. The female accipiter is often much larger than the male.

Harriers have a facial disc, like owls, that helps them hear their prey. Most show color differences between the adult male and female birds.

Buteos are found nearly worldwide in open country and some forested areas. They have broad wings with deeply slit wing tips; short, stout legs with short toes.

There is a miscellaneous group of hawks that do not fit into the other hawk groups. Most of these birds live in the tropics.

links.title: Northern Goshawk
links.description: Learn where this accipter lives, what it eats, how it hunts, and why they are used in falconry. See photos and take a quiz.

links.title: Swainson's Hawk
links.description: The Peregrine Fund tells where this buteo lives, what it eats, how it hunts, and what its name means. See photos and take a quiz.

links.title: White-tailed Hawk
links.description: All About Birds gives cool facts about this buteo's wings. Learn where they live, how they sound, and how their colors change.

links.title: Red-shouldered Hawk
links.description: All About Birds tells where the five species of this buteo live, how they are different from each other, what they sound like, and some cool facts.

451390.title: Harriers
451390.description: Harriers are birds of prey, related to hawks, eagles, and kites. They fly low over meadows and marshes and hunt or harry (bother) small animals or birds. Typical harriers have long wings that they hold in a shallow V in their low flight. They also have distinct male and female plumages. The female is generally larger than the male. Harriers hunt other birds, hares, rabbits, rats, mice, lizards, frogs, fish, and insects. Because they rely heavily on material already dead (carrion), harriers are often killed by cars as they feed on roadsides.

links.title: Northern Harrier
links.description: Texas Parks and Wildlife tells why they are like an owl, how many mates they have, what habitat they prefer, and where they live.

links.title: RSPB: Hen Harrier
links.description: Learn where they live, what they eat, when to see them in the UK and why hunters don't like them. Hear their call and watch videos from the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds.

links.title: Wingspan National Bird of Prey Centre: Swamp Harrier
links.description: Tells what this New Zealand raptor eats, where it nests, why it's protected and hear its call.

451391.title: Kites
451391.description:
Kites are not aggressive or extremely predatory hunters. Instead, they eat small animals, insects, snails, or scavenge dead animals and garbage.

These raptors have short lower legs, relatively weak feet with short toes, long, often pointed wings, and a squared tail that may be notched or forked. Most kites are social and often nest in colonies.

The male and female birds in this group tend to be the same size, and often share the duties of nest building, incubation, and feeding the young.

links.title: Mississippi Kite
links.description: Learn about this social raptor, what they eat, how they hunt, and where they nest and spend the winter. From Texas Parks and Wildlife.

links.title: Snail Kite
links.description: Find out where this tropical raptor lives, what it eats, how it builds its nest, and other interesting facts. See photos and take a quiz. From The Peregrine Fund.

451388.title: New World Vultures
451388.description:
New World vultures inhabit North and South America.

They have an raised hind toe for walking. Except for hisses and grunts, they are almost silent because they have no voice box.

This group of birds includes the Andean and California condors, and the Black and Turkey Vultures.

Some believe that New World vultures are more closely related to storks than hawks and eagles.

links.title: Andean Condor
links.description: Explains how big they are, where they live, what they eat, how they nest, and interesting facts. See photos and take a quiz. From The Peregrine Fund.

links.title: California Condor
links.description: The Peregrine Fund tells where this bird lives, what it eats, where it nests, and why it is endangered. See photos and take a quiz.

links.title: Turkey Vulture
links.description: Read about where these raptors live and migrate, what they eat, how they got their name, and interesting facts. See photos and take a quiz. From The Peregrine Fund.

451384.title: Ospreys
451384.description:
Ospreys are large, powerful raptors.

Although it looks like a hawk, it has narrow, angled wings. The structure of its feet and claws is so peculiar that it has been placed in its own subfamily, the Pandioninae.

Unlike other raptors, the Osprey has four equal toes. The outer one is reversible, enabling the bird to seize its prey with two toes pointing forwards and two pointing backwards.

links.title: Osprey
links.description: Explains what this raptor eats, where it hunts, how it builds its nest, and interesting facts. See photos and take a quiz. From The Peregrine Fund.

451405.title: Ratites
451405.description:
Ratites are birds in the order Struthioniformes who are unable to fly.

Birds in this group include cassowaries, emus, kiwis, moas, ostrich, and rheas.

451367.title: Shorebirds
451367.description:
Shorebirds are a group of birds that live on beaches, grasslands, and wetlands. They often have long bills, legs, and toes that help with wading in the water. Because many build their nests in the sand, most have earth-colored feathers to help them hide.

Birds in this group include plovers, oystercatchers, curlews, avocets, stilts, and sandpipers. They are migratory birds, which means they travel to different places when the weather changes.

As global warming, pollution, and oil spills damage wetlands and beaches, shorebirds are becoming endangered. Because they travel long distances, any area along their path that is destroyed affects the birds.

links.title: American Avocet
links.description: Texas Parks and Wildlife explains what this shorebird looks like, where it lives, how it eats, and why it is protected.

451368.title: Curlews
451368.description:
Curlews are shorebirds with long, down-curved bills that help them search for food in mud or very soft ground. Many migrate long distances, from as far north as Siberia to Australia and farther.

There are eight different species of curlew: the Whimbrel, Bristle-thighed, Eurasian, Eastern, Little, and Long-billed. The Slender-billed Curlew is critically endangered.

The Eskimo Curlew may be extinct. The last confirmed sighting was in 1962. A book and animated movie, Last of the Curlews, tell the story of this bird that may have been seen by Columbus when he reached North America.

links.title: Eskimo Curlew (Numenius  borealis)
links.description: Tells what they look like, why they are endangered, where they live, and how they migrate.

451371.title: Godwits
451371.description:
Godwits are shorebirds with straight or slightly up-turned bills that help them pick up insects and crustaceans. The females are usually much larger than the males.

There are four different species of godwit: the Black-tailed, Hudsonian, Bar-tailed, and Marbled.

451369.title: Oystercatchers
451369.description:
Oystercatchers are large, noisy birds, with strong bills used for smashing or prying open mollusks, or pointed bills used to dig for worms.

These shorebirds live on coasts all over the world, except for the polar regions. They are all-black, black and white, or brown and white in appearance.

There are eleven species, including the Chatham Islands Oystercatcher which is critically endangered.

links.title: American Oystercatcher

451370.title: Plovers
451370.description: Plovers (family Charadriidae) live all over the world, from arctic tundra to tropical sandbars. There are 66 different species in this family of birds. Some look alike; others are very different. Because people like to live and play where the plovers live and play, many species are becoming threatened or endangered.

links.title: Western Snowy Plover

451372.title: Stone-Curlews
451372.description:
Stone-curlews, also called Thick-knees, are medium to large shorebirds that live in warm, tropical areas. Although related to plovers and avocets, these birds prefer to live and hunt on dry land. They have strong black or yellow black bills, and large yellow eyes.

There are nine species, including Stone Curlew, Bush Stone-curlew, Beach Stone-curlew, Great Thick-knee, Senegal Thick-knee, Double-striped Thick-knee, Peruvian Thick-knee, Water Dikkop, and Spotted Dikkop.

These birds are named for their songs, which sound like curlews and for their large knee joints. Hunting at night, they eat insects and other invertebrates. Larger birds also eat crustaceans and small lizards.

links.title: Stone-curlew
links.description: Wikipedia entry tells about this family of birds. Includes the nine species, what they look like, where they live and nest, and what they eat.

links.title: Stone-curlew
links.description: Read about this red-listed shorebird, where it lives, what it eats, why it is threatened and what is being done to help. See videos. [Audio/video requires free Quicktime download.]

451373.title: Bush Stone-Curlews
451373.description:
Bush Stone-curlews, also called Bush Thick-knees, are large shorebirds that live throughout Australia. Although related to plovers and avocets, these birds prefer to live and hunt on dry land. They have strong black bills, and large yellow eyes.

These birds are named for their songs, which sound like curlews and for their large knee joints. Hunting at night, they eat insects, crustaceans and small lizards.

links.description: Learn about this shorebird, also called Bush Stone-curlew. Includes its appearance, diet, nesting habits, and how and where it is threatened.

451394.title: Songbirds
451394.description: Birds classified in the order Passeriformes are often called "songbirds." They also are called "perching birds." This group includes many of the familiar birds of woodlands, yards, and gardens.   Not all "Songbirds" are known for pretty songs.

451398.title: Wading Birds
451398.description:
Wading birds are part of a larger group called Colonial-nesting waterbirds. These birds all gather in colonies at nesting time and get most or all of their food from the water.

Herons, egrets, bitterns, spoonbills, and storks are all members of this group. What makes them different than seabirds is that they feed in fresh water.

As global warming and pollution damage wetlands and beaches, wading birds are becoming endangered. Because they migrate long distances, any area along their path that is destroyed affects the birds.

links.title: The Ciconiiformes
links.description: Offers an introduction to bitterns, ibises, herons, spoonbills, and storks. Includes differences in habitat, feeding habits, and how wading birds are threatened.

451399.title: Egrets
451399.description:
Egrets are members of a large family of wading birds that includes 65 species of egrets, night-herons, typical herons, tiger-herons, and bitterns. Their long necks, longer than their bodies, are retracted during flight, which is how watchers can tell them from storks and cranes.

These great hunters feed on fish, frogs, crayfish and snakes. Some stir up the mud with their feet to attract prey. When feeding in flocks, it is common to see egrets leap-frog over each other, or plunge into the water.

The biggest threat to egrets in the past was the demand for their decorative feathers. Although most species are recovering, the destruction of wetlands has added a modern threat.

links.title: Great Egret
links.description: Read about the largest of the Australian egrets. Includes description, food and feeding, distribution and habitat, and breeding facts.

451400.title: Herons
451400.description:
Herons are members of a large family of wading birds that includes 65 species of night-herons, typical herons, tiger-herons, egrets, and bitterns. They fly with their long necks retracted, which is how watchers can tell them from storks and cranes.

Great hunters, the Black Heron spreads its wings like a canopy and waits for prey to seek shelter in the shade. Other herons flick bits of feathers on the water or stir up the muddy bottom to attract prey.

In February 2005, a Canadian scientist announced that he had a method to measure birds' intelligence, based on the ways they hunt. Herons were named among the most intelligent birds based on this scale.

links.title: White-faced Heron
links.description: Brief article explains what they look like. Includes where they live, what they eat, and how they build a nest.

451402.title: Storks
451402.description:
Storks are all members of the group of birds called Wading birds. What makes them different than seabirds is that they feed in fresh water.

As global warming and pollution damage wetlands and beaches, wading birds are becoming endangered. Because they migrate long distances, any area along their path that is destroyed affects the birds.

links.title: Black-necked Stork/Jabiru
links.description: Provides information about the only stork found in Australia. Includes description, habitat, diet, and breeding.

links.title: Order Anseriformes (Waterfowl)

451378.title: Ducks
451378.description:
Ducks part of a group of birds called waterfowl, because they are normally found in places with water like ponds, streams and rivers.

Male ducks are called drakes and usually have more colorful feathers than the females. These birds have webbed feet that act like paddles and water-proof feathers that help keep their skin dry and warm.

451381.title: Geese
451381.description:
Geese are the middle-sized waterfowl; larger than ducks and smaller than swans. Many birds have 'goose' in their name, but only some of them are true geese.

The male is often called a gander; the female is the goose; and the young are called goslings. Geese on the ground are a gaggle, but in flight they are called a wedge or skein.

451379.title: Seaducks
451379.description:
Sea ducks are a tribe of waterfowl (Mergini) that live in the northern hemisphere. They are also called diving ducks, because they dive under the water to catch food.

There are 20 species of sea ducks, including eiders, scoters, smew, mergansers, and goldeneyes. More than half of these species are threatened or endangered. One, the Labrador Duck, is extinct.

451380.title: Swans
451380.description:
Swans are the largest of the waterfowl and, some believe, the most beautiful. Males are called cobs, females are pens, and the young are cygnets.

There are nine species of swans. The Whooper, Trumpeter, Tundra, Mute, Bewick's, and Jankowski's live in the northern hemisphere; the Black-necked, Black, and Coscoroba live in the southern.

The most commonly seen member of the group is the Mute Swan. Its curving neck that has the most vertebra (23) of any bird.

451404.description: There are several species of woodpecker in many countries.

451540.title: Mammals
451540.description: The mammals category houses sites about all mammals that exist, including marine mammals.  Marine mammals should not be listed in the Marine Life category.          There are a total of 4,060 mammals all together, living species. There are some defining characteristics that make a mammal a mammal.          1) Mammary glands are what makes a mammal a mammal.  It is responsible for the process of lactation, or the production of milk. This helps mothers feed their young.        2) The presence of hair or fur for the purpose of insulation is also a defining characteristic. It helps maintain temperature.

451613.title: Cougars
451613.description:
Cougars have more names than probably any other big cat. Mountain lion, puma, painter, and catamount are just some of them.

Found in a range from northern Canada to the southern tip of South America, the color of their coat is different in each area. They live in mountains, forests, steppes, and grasslands.

Years of hunting and destruction of cougar habitats, has left so few in some areas that they are critically endangered. Many countries now protect them.

451623.title: Primates
451623.description:
What is a primate?

A primate is a classification of biology used to group several similar animal species together. Probably the most recognizable to kids are the monkey and the human. Yes, you are a primate.

All primates have nails, hooves or claws. A lot of things that have claws are not primates though, like birds. Primates also have a clavicle, also known as a collar bone. Another feature of the primate is that their innermost digit (finger) is opposable. What this means is that the thumb can be used to pick things up. Imagine how hard it would be to pick things up without your thumb.

451321.title: Measurement
451321.description: To measure is to compare the dimensions, quantity, or capacity with a standard. There are several systems of measurement. The two used most often are called the English and the metric systems (also called SI, or The International System).   In the United States, the English system is used most often. While most other parts of the world use the metric system.   The basic units used in the metric system are:  Length in meters (m), Mass in kilograms (kg), and Time in seconds (s).   The basic units used in the metric system are:  Length in yards (yd), Weight in pounds (lb), and Time in Seconds (s).   The English units of measurement have many drawbacks: the most significant is in the complexity of converting from one unit to another, such as from yards to feet.

451296.title: Atoms, Nuclei and Particles
451296.description: An atom is a submicroscopic structure found in all ordinary matter. It is the smallest unit of an element to retain all the chemical properties of that element. Most atoms are composed of three types of massive subatomic particles which govern their external properties: electrons, protons, and neutrons. Together, protons and neutrons form the nucleus of an atom, which is surrounded by the electrons. But protons, and neutrons are actually composite particles, made up of quarks, as well as other particles such as photons and neutrinos which are produced copiously in the sun. However, most of the particles that have been discovered and studied are not encountered under normal earth conditions; they are produced in cosmic rays and during scattering processes in particle accelerators. Physics branches devoted to the study of atoms, nuclei and particles, their properties and associated phenomena such as radioactivity, nuclear fission and nuclear fusion, are, for example, quantum mechanics and nuclear physics.

451311.title: Electricity and Magnetism
451311.description: This category is about electric and the magnetic fields. A non-zero electric field is produced by the presence of electrically charged particles, and gives rise to the electric force; this is the force that causes static electricity and drives the flow of electric charge (electric current) in electrical conductors. The magnetic field, on the other hand, can be produced by the motion of electric charges, or electric current, and gives rise to the magnetic force associated with magnets. The term "electromagnetism" comes from the fact that the electric and magnetic fields generally cannot be described independently of one another. A changing magnetic field produces an electric field (this is the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction, which underlies the operation of electrical generators, induction motors, and transformers). Similarly, a changing electric field generates a magnetic field.

451320.title: Energy
451320.description: In physics, energy is a fundamental quantity that every physical system possesses. Energy of physical system in a certain given state is defined as the amount of work (W) needed to change the state of the system from some initial position to a specific or final position. Energy is found in different forms: Kinetic energy: the energy of moving objects; Thermal energy: the energy associated with heat; Sound energy: the energy of compression waves; Electrical energy: the energy of moving charged particles; Potential Energy: the energy that an object has due to position; also known as stored energy; Chemical energy: the stored energy of chemical substances; Nuclear energy: the stored energy of the atomic nucleus and Radiant energy: the energy of electromagnetic waves, including light. Energy can be readily transformed from one form into another; for instance, using a battery to power an electrical heater converts chemical energy into electrical energy, which is then converted into thermal energy. Also, energy could be transformed in matter and vice versa as the theory of relativity states.

451294.description: Thermodynamics is a branch of physics that studies the effects of temperature on physical systems at the macroscopic scale. 451307.title: Light and Optics
451307.description: Optics is a branch of physics that describes the behavior and properties of light and the interaction of light with matter. Optics explains and is illuminated by optical phenomena. The field of optics usually describes the behavior of visible, infrared and ultraviolet light; however because light is an electromagnetic wave, analogous phenomena occur in X-rays, microwaves, radio waves, and other forms of electromagnetic radiation. Optics can thus be regarded as a sub-field of electromagnetism. Some optical phenomena depend on the quantum nature of light and as such some areas of optics are also related to quantum mechanics. Optics has two primary branches: physical optics and geometrical optics.

451313.title: Gravity
451313.description: Gravity is the force of attraction between massive particles. Weight is determined by the mass of an object and its location in a gravitational field. Gravity, simply put, is acceleration. F=ma means that there must be a force that causes a mass to accelerate. For a rocket ship, that is the rocket motor. For the earth, that is the compression of the mass between something on the surface of the earth and the earth's center of mass. While a great deal is known about the properties of gravity, the ultimate cause of the gravitational force remains an open question. General relativity is the most successful theory of gravitation to date. It postulates that mass and energy curve space-time, resulting in the phenomenon known as gravity.

451310.title: Sound and Acoustics
451310.description: Sound is vibration, as perceived by the sense of hearing. Vibrations usually travel to our ears through the air; the ear converts them into nerve impulses sent to our brains, where the impulses become sound. In more technical language, sound "is an alternation in pressure, particle displacement, or particle velocity propagated in an elastic material" (Olson 1957) or series of mechanical compressions and rarefactions or longitudinal waves that successively propagate through media that are at least a little compressible (solid, liquid or gas but not vacuum). In sound waves parts of matter (molecules or groups of molecules) move in a direction of the spreading of the disturbance (as opposite to transversal waves). The cause of sound waves is called the source of waves, e.g. a violin string vibrating upon being bowed or plucked. A sound wave is usually represented graphically by a wavy, horizontal line; the upper part of the wave (the crest) indicates a compression and the lower part (the trough) indicates a rarefaction.

451317.title: Structure and Properties of Matter
451317.description: Matter occupies space and has mass. In bulk, matter can exist in several different phases, according to particle density and energy density or alternatively pressure and temperature. These phases include gases, plasmas, liquids, fluids, superfluids, solids, and Bose-Einstein condensate and have their particular properties. As circumstances change, matter may change from one phase into another. These phenomena are called phase transitions, and their energetics are studied in the field of thermodynamics. In small quantities, matter can exhibit properties that are entirely different from those of bulk material. Matter constitutes the observable Universe. It can be converted to energy (see annihilation), and vice versa - can be created out of energy (see matter creation) and undergo other formations and alterations.

451701.description: Erosion is the displacement of solids such as soil, mud, rocks by wind, water, ice, gravity, or living organisms.

links.title: Dirtmeister: Erosion
links.description: Investigate and report the effects of erosion.

links.title: Soil: Erosion and Conservation
links.description: How the soil is being damaged by rain, gravity, and wind. Plus why we should be concerned.

links.title: The Magic School Bus Rocks and Rolls
links.description: Experiment with clay and water to see the effects of erosion.

links.title: Our Weathering/Erosion Experiment
links.description: A backyard experiment that you can do too, with the help of your parents.

451702.title: Wind
451702.description: Wind erosion is the movement of rock by the wind. Trees, shrubs or other vegetation are often planted by farmers to reduce wind erosion.

links.title: Reading the Environment in the Sand
links.description: Includes information on how researchers can estimate how much wind it takes to erode rocks.

links.title: An Introduction to Wind Erosion Control
links.description: How humans can decrease the effects of wind erosion.

links.title: Earth Floor
links.description: Learn about the earth by reading short articles on plate tectonics, cycles, geologic time, adaptation and more.

links.title: USGS Learning Web
links.description: Learn how Biology, Geology, Hydrology, and Geography can help us understand our changing world.

links.title: Geologic and Paleontologic Cook Book
links.description: The Kentucky Geological Survey offers recipes for appetizers, desserts and other food that help to explain earth-science concepts.

links.title: Geography4Kids
links.description: Learn about earth structure, atmosphere, natural energies, water resources, living things, climate and cycles.  Page includes photos and explanation of terms.

links.title: Yellowstone National Park - For Kids
links.description: Learn about Yellowstone National Park with games and activities like the Animal Alphabet Book, the Yellowstone Coloring Book and a Scavenger Hunt.

links.title: Grand Canyon Explorer: Geology of the Grand Canyon
links.description: Explains how layers of the Grand Canyon were formed over a period of about 2 million years. Many illustrations. Gives a couple different theories about some of the details.

links.title: Smithsonian Department of Mineral Sciences
links.description: Explore a photo gallery of gems, volcanoes, rocks, minerals and meteorites. Offers research, collections and exhibits.

links.title: Magnificant Mulu
links.description: Find out more about the mysteries of the Mulu cave system in Malaysia.  Discover how many animal and plant species rely on these caves and view some pictures of limestone formations.

links.title: Virtual Cave
links.description: Photographs of caves from all over the world both underwater and underground.  Includes close-up shots and descriptions of the different plants, animals, and minerals found in each.

links.title: Life Along the Faultline
links.description: Investigates life and science along California's fault lines. The site includes exclusive video from the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake.

links.title: Thirteen: Savage Rest: Restless Planet
links.description: Sections on learning from earthquakes, predicting quakes, and engineering quake-resistant buildings. Uses Flash animation and Quicktime video.

links.title: UCGS Earthquake Hazards Program
links.description: Find lots of information on earthquakes. Includes maps of recent activity.

links.title: Seismic Waves
links.description: Basic introduction to seismic waves and how we use them to understand more about the inside of the earth.

links.title: USGS: Earthquakes for Kids
links.description: Site features puzzles, games, science fair ideas, the online activity links, and virtual earthquake fly-bys.

links.title: Seismology Facts for Kids
links.description: Fun facts on the study of earthquakes and the waves they create.

451760.title: Geologic Time
451760.description:
Also known as "geological time", this refers to the period covering the physical formation and development of Earth, especially prior to human history.
Adapted from The American Heritage® Dictionary of the English Language, Fourth Edition

links.title: Geologic Time Scale

links.title: Comprehending Geological Time
links.description: An interactive tool to calculate time periods and human history in terms of different measurement scales such as a meter, a day or a million years.

links.title: Earth Floor: Geologic Time
links.description: Explains how the age of the earth is divided up into periods of time, and provides simple definitions and illustrations of the different names.

451761.title: Glaciers and Ice Ages
451761.description: Glaciers are slow-moving "rivers of ice", and they give some idea of what the Earth looked like during one of the Ice Ages.

links.title: Illinois State Museum: Explore the Ice Age Midwest
links.description: A museum exhibit explains what they are, and how and why they occur. Includes animation of the retreating ice in North America.

links.title: Orbital Changes: The Ice Ages

links.title: Wikipedia: Ice Ages
links.description: Encyclopedia article outlines the theories used to explain the ice ages, and the effects of the interglacial periods.

links.title: Tongass National Forest: Glaciers and Icefields
links.description: Heading north to Alaska means going to glacier heaven! Discover how glaciers are formed and just what glaciers do.

links.title: Cracking the Ice Age
links.description: Web site related to the NOVA television program about the big sweep and panorama of the Ice Age. Links to other resources.

links.title: All About Glaciers
links.description: Get the scoop on everything you wanted to know about glaciers.

links.title: Glaciers
links.description: Learn what a glacier is, how it forms, how it moves, and what types of glaciers exist in the world.

links.description: Looks at the fossils from the La Brea area to get an idea of what life was like during the ice age.

links.title: A Quick Background to the Last Ice Age
links.description: Features a summary of the sequence of events for the last 130,000 years, from the time the ice started melting.

links.title: An Introduction to Plate Tectonics
links.description: Find out how and why certain plates move and learn some of the theories that scientists have used to explain these movements.

links.title: Quia - Java Games
links.description: Contains games and activities that help users learn some terms related to the study of plate tectonics and continental drift.

451764.title: Tsunamis
451764.description:
Tsunami is a Japanese word represented by two characters: "tsu" and "nami." The character "tsu" means harbor, and the character "nami" means wave. In the past, tsunamis were often referred to as "tidal waves." The term "tidal wave" is a misnomer. Tides are the result of gravitational influences of the moon, sun, and planets. Tsunamis are not caused by the tides and are unrelated to the tides.
from the National Tsunami Hazard Mitigation Program.

links.title: Pacific Tsunami Museum
links.description: Promotes public education about tsunamis for the people of Hawaii and the Pacific Region. Includes answers to commonly asked questions and tsunami photographs.

links.title: Savage Earth: Waves of Destruction
links.description: Highlights include animated illustrations, articles, an "Ask the Experts" section, photographs, and video downloads.

links.title: Tsunami: The Great Wave
links.description: Discusses what tsunamis are, what causes them, and how warning systems can help save lives.

links.title: Wikipedia - 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake

links.title: Tsunami WebQuest 2004

links.title: U.S. National Tsunami Warning Center
links.description: Issues tsunami messages to notify emergency managers, the public, and other partners about the potential for a tsunami following a possible tsunami-generating event. Has additional seismic analysis, water-level measurements, tsunami forecast model results, and historical tsunami information.

links.title: Tsunami!
links.description: Answers many questions about the topic. What does tsunami mean? How are they created? What happens to a tsunami as it approaches land?

links.title: NOVA: Volcano's Deadly Warning
