links.description: Contains information related to the volcano Mt. Etna including formation, location, history, consequences, benefits, preventative measures, and comparison with other volcanoes.

links.title: Cascades Volcano Observatory
links.description: Information about and photos of the Cascades volcanoes, Mount Saint Helens updates, and volcano monitoring and hazards information.

links.title: Volcano Under the City
links.description: Explore some of the worst volcanic disasters of the past four centuries, find out what features make an unquiet volcano tick, and learn if it is possible to forecast volcanic eruptions.

links.title: Lecture Notes
links.description: Learn about the lava flows, pyroclastics, and Mount Saint Helens.

links.title: VolcanoWorld
links.description: Includes stories about volcanoes by children's author Jane Kurtz, school project ideas, legends, virtual field trips, and games.

links.title: Volcanology Facts For Kids

451763.title: Image Galleries

links.description: Learn more about aquifers by looking at South Dakota's aquifers. Discover what an aquifer is, where they can be found, and its significance to humans in general.

451708.title: Natural Disasters and Hazards
451708.description: For sites concerning hurricanes, earthquakes, tornadoes, avalanches, floods, landslides, and other natural disasters.

451712.title: Avalanches
451712.description: An avalanche results from a large mass of snow and ice suddenly slipping from its position and moving rapidly down a slope.

links.description: Facts and figures from the National Snow and Ice Data Center. Includes safety advice and an explanation of the danger scale.

links.description: Questions and answers about what an avalanche is, and the dangers of them.

links.title: Colorado Avalanche Information Center
links.description: Provides avalanche forecasts and warnings for Colorado.  Includes accident reports and educational resources.

links.description: Illustrated explanations of how they are formed, and why they behave differently.

links.description: Article warns of the dangers of avalanches when skiing.

451711.title: Bushfires and Wildfires
451711.description: Different terms are used around the world to refer to these fires, which may be caused by humans or natural forces like lightening, and which often cause a lot of damage. They may occur in forests, grasslands, or farming areas, and sometimes burn for days or weeks before being brought under control.

links.title: BushFires Clearly Explained
links.description: Describes how they start, what effect they have on the environment, and what people can do to manage them properly. Includes diagrams of the way a bushfire develops.

links.title: Canberra's Bushfire Pictures
links.description: Galleries of photographs taken during the fires which destroyed forests, homes, and farms around the national capital of Australia in January 2003.

451709.title: Floods
451709.description: Floods are a common natural disaster, and can be caused by excessive rain, a break in the wall of a dam or levee, or by a change in sea level such as a tsunami.

links.title: Hot Science: The River's Gift
links.description: Questions and photographs show how flooding rivers can be a benefit to the surrounding land.

links.title: Dealing with the Deluge
links.description: Shows how efforts to control the flooding of the major rivers of the world is not always successful. Includes photographs and diagrams of what happens.

links.title: Flooding on the Red River of the North
links.description: This area of North Dakota and Minnesota in the United States has experienced a lot of floods. Photographs and diagrams explain why, and show the damage caused over the years.

links.title: Guardian: Floods in Europe
links.description: Pictures and stories of the floods which damaged large areas of Central and Eastern Europe in 2002.

451710.title: Landslides
451710.description: Landslides can occur after heavy rain, if a retaining structure gives way, or if a weakness develops in the ground. They are called mudslides if the soil is saturated with water.

links.description: Learn what a lahar is, where they occur, and the destruction they cause.

451687.title: Tides
451687.description: The periodic rise and fall of the sea level under the gravitational pull of the moon.

links.title: NOVA:  Sinking City of Venice
links.description: Program about the threat that Venice is under from rising tides.

links.title: What are Tides?
links.description: Brief definition concerning the rise and fall of the tides.

links.title: Enchanted Learning: Tides
links.description: Brief description and illustrations about what causes the tide to rise and fall.

451688.title: Tidal Bores
451688.description: A high wave caused by tidal flow into a narrow opening or estuary. A tidal bore is a naturally occurring event that should not be confused with a tsunami. The bore is caused when  an incoming tide rushes up a river. There are only 100 places around the world where this natural phenomenon occurs.

links.title: Wikipedia: Tidal Bore
links.description: Provides description and links to various known tidal bores in the world.

451767.title: Prehistoric Times
451767.description:
Includes the development of life on earth up to the time of modern man, as well as changes on the Earth itself.

"Prehistory" is the period of history before writing was invented and records kept. The term was coined by Daniel Wilson in 1851. The study of prehistory is concerned with events and developments for which material evidence survives. Adapted from The Columbia Electronic Encyclopedia, Sixth Edition

links.title: Prehistory in the Electronic Passport
links.description: Brief history of early man's culture and development.

links.title: Prehistoric Man by History Link 101

links.description: Broadband documentary offers a journey through human evolution; also includes activities and lesson plans.

links.title: Mysteries of Çatalhöyük
links.description: An interactive tour of this archaeological dig in Turkey. Includes a timeline and photographs of the project, and details of the techniques used.

links.title: The Midwestern U.S. 16,000 Years Ago

links.title: Mary Leakey:  Unearthing History
links.description: Profile of Mary Leakey from the Scientific American.

links.description: Features collections, illustrations, and fact sheets of extinct fauna.

links.title: Prehistory Facts For Kids
links.description: Prehistory is the long time before people started to write things down. The word comes from two Ancient Greek words: "pro" (meaning "before") and "historia" (meaning "history").

links.title: Stone Age Facts For Kids
links.description: The Stone Age was a very long time in history when people mostly used stone to make their tools.

links.title: Bronze Age Facts For Kids
links.description: The Bronze Age was a time in history when people started making tools and weapons from a special metal mix called bronze.

links.title: Iron Age Facts For Kids
links.description: The Iron Age was a time in history when people started using iron to make tools and weapons.

451771.title: Animals
451771.description:
Animals existed for hundreds of millions of years before there were any humans, so we know about them only through evidence left behind, by careful study of their descendents, or in some cases, by studying living examples which have changed little since prehistoric times.

It seems that the first animals were those which lived in the sea, followed by the group known as dinosaurs, and much later, birds and mammals.

links.title: Parrot Fossil from the Cretaceous Pushes Back Origin of Modern Land Birds
links.description: Berkeleyan, the faculty staff newspaper of the University of California, talks about the discovery of the oldest fossil from a modern land bird.

links.title: Ichthyornis
links.description: Description of the discovery of a toothed flying sea bird from the Late Cretaceous.

links.title: Fossil Record of the Aves
links.description: An overview of notable bird fossils.

links.title: BBC: Hesperornis
links.description: A large flightless swimming bird from the Late Cretaceous is described.

451773.title: Archaeopteryx
451773.description: Archaeopteryx meaning "ancient feather" is considered the earliest and most primitive known bird.

links.title: The Canadian Museum of Nature: Archaeopteryx

links.title: Archaeopteryx

451774.title: Dinosaurs
451774.description: Dinosaurs hold a special fascination for children. This category contains sites that are geared toward kids ages 3-18.

links.title: Dinosaur Questions and Answers

links.title: NOVA Online/Curse of T. rex

451783.title: Ankylosaurus

451775.title: Giganotosaurus
451775.description: Giganotosaurus ("giant southern lizard") lived during the Late Cretaceous period. It is one of the biggest known terrestrial carnivores.

451785.description: The parasaurolophus was a plant eating dinosaur with a distinctive head shape. It had a six-foot long curved crest sticking out from the back of the head.

links.description: Contains a fact sheet, information on its anatomy, classification and when it lived.

451777.description: The velociraptor was a small meat eating dinosaur, about less than 2 meters long and a meter tall. (Or about 6 feet long and two and a half feet tall.)

451787.title: Mammals
451787.description: The earliest mammal identified so far is from about 45 million years ago, but we are more familiar with the ones from 10,000 to 70,000 years ago. These co-existed with the first humans, and are better known because of cave paintings, mummified carcasses, tools made from bones, and other remains.

links.description: A detailed and illustrated guide to the first 10 million years of their evolution.

links.description: Hyperlinked encyclopedia article discusses genera, evolutionary tree, use of the canine teeth, and species.

451786.title: Marine Life
451786.description:
The earliest animals lived in the sea, and preserved and fossilised remains have provided a lot of information about them, and about conditions on Earth at the time. Many of the fossils discovered so far have been found on land, sometimes hundreds of miles from the sea.
Some present-day marine creatures have changed very little from prehistoric times.

links.title: Reptiles of the Ancient Seas
links.description: The Museum of Unnatural Mystery explains about these creatures with the aid of pictures and animations.

links.title: A Moment in Time
links.description: An illustrated story about an attack on a mosasaur by a prehistoric giant shark, based on the damage to bones found in Kansas, USA. Includes photographs of the fossil specimens.

links.title: New Zealand's Ancient Marine Reptiles
links.description: Information about prehistoric marine reptiles of New Zealand, where, whom, when and what was found. Where in New Zealand to see fossil material displayed, and suggested reading material.

links.description: Many pages of information on mosasaurs, plesiosaurs and other fossils found in Kansas and the Midwest.

links.title: Plesiosaur Directory
links.description: Introduction to the group including taxonomy, reconstructions, and original artwork.

451790.title: Fossils
451790.description:
The remains or imprints of plants or animals preserved from prehistoric times by the operation of natural conditions. Fossils are found in sedimentary rock, asphalt deposits, and coal and sometimes in amber and certain other materials. The scientific study of fossils is paleontology.
From The Columbia Electronic Encyclopedia, Sixth Edition

links.title: The Paleontology Portal
links.description: Shows photos of fossils of different types. Browse by location, time period or type. Produced by the University of California Museum of Paleontology, the Paleontological Society, the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology, and the United States Geological Survey.

links.title: Jurassic Ammonites
links.description: A detailed description of discoveries in France, with illustrations, history, photographs and a section on myths and legends. [English and French]

451768.title: People
451768.description:
This term is not well defined, but is often used to refer to the development of human culture around 100,000 to 200,000 years ago. Discussion continues between anthropologists, theologians, paleontologists and archeologists about when the terms "human" and "modern man" can be applied.
This category represents sites concerning early societies which had some form of culture in terms of tool making, painting, burial rituals or other activities for which evidence has survived.

links.title: Neanderthals on Trial
links.description: Website is companion to NOVA documentary which explores the ancestral roots of humans.

451769.title: Cave Paintings
451769.description: This is a form of expression used for tens of thousands of years, and varies from rough outlines of hands to stylised depictions of animals and people.

links.title: Paintings, Engravings and Sculptures
links.description: Illustrated articles about famous cave paintings in France and rock engravings in Norway.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cave Painting
links.description: Encyclopedia article describes the different discoveries and the conclusions that have been made about the people who created them.

links.title: The Cave of Lascaux
links.description: Interactive exploration of this prehistoric site, with illustrations of the artwork on its walls and roof. [English, French, German and Spanish]

451770.title: Tools
451770.description: One of the activities that helps to define the transition from human ancestors to humans is the creation of tools to assist in hunting and daily life. Early tools were probably made of wood, and no longer exist, but those created from bone, antler, stone, or flint have been found in many locations and from many different periods.

links.title: Tools from the Stone Age
links.description: Features illustrated articles on making flint tools, musical instruments, spear throwing and decorative objects.

451713.title: The Atmosphere
451713.description: For sites concerning any of the features of the Earth's atmosphere, including the weather.

451718.description: El Niño and La Niña are disruptions of the ocean-atmosphere system in the tropical Pacific having important consequences for weather around the globe.   La Niña is characterized by unusually cold ocean temperatures in the Equatorial Pacific, compared to El Niño, which is characterized by unusually warm ocean temperatures in the Equatorial Pacific.   ENSO is the generic term for these phenomena.

451717.title: Urban Heat Island Effect
451717.description: An urban heat island is a city that is much warmer than its surroundings. It can affect local weather patterns, and maybe global patterns (such as global warming) as well.

451719.title: Optical Effects

451720.description: A sun dog is an atmospheric optical phenomenon caused by reflection and refraction of sunlight by ice crystals that make up cirrus clouds. When attempting to look at sun dog, do not look directly at the sun.

links.title: Wikipedia: Sun Dog

451734.description: A blizzard is a winter storm where lots of snow falls during an extended period of time. Usually there are "whiteout" conditions, which means you can't see because everything looks white.

links.title: Wikipedia: Haboob

451725.description: Weather prediction, or forecasting, is the attempt to say what the weather will be in the future based on what the weather is like today.

links.title: Weather Prediction Education
links.description: Browse through forecasting techniques, weather forecasting,  and forecasting tools.

links.title: Scholastic: Predicting the Weather
links.description: Frequently asked questions about weather prediction.

links.title: Weather Forecasting: Online Meteorology Guide
links.description: Looks at different forecasting methods, and how to predict temperature and precipitation.

451726.title: Image Galleries
451726.description: This category contains pictures galleries of the weather, from sunsets to thunderstorms, to snow. Sites which only feature a few pictures of only one weather topic should be listed in that particular topic.

links.title: Weather Underground: Current Weather Related Photos
links.description: Contains weather and other outdoor photographs.

links.title: Weather Photography
links.description: A large collection of weather and atmospheric photography.

links.title: David Blanchard Photography
links.description: Gallery contains thunderstorms, lightning, and tornadoes.

451753.title: Instruments
451753.description: This category is for sites which describe the instruments scientists use to help predict the weather.

links.title: Weather Instruments
links.description: Short encyclopedia entries for several different weather instruments.

links.title: Weather Instruments
links.description: Learn about the instruments scientists use to predict the weather.

451754.title: Make Your Own
451754.description:
This category is for sites that describe how to build weather stations. Types of instruments typically found in weather stations include:
  • Barometer: Measures air pressure
  • Rain Gauge: Measures precipitation
  • Thermometer: Measures temperature
  • Wind Vane: Measures wind direction
  • Anemometer: Measures wind speed

links.title: Weather Scope: Make a Weather Station
links.description: Directions to build barometer, rain gauge, thermometer, wind vane and anemometer, with discussion questions, how to record measurements, and optional homework.

links.title: American Museum of Natural History: Make Your Own Weather Station
links.description: Get your parents to help you build your own barometer, wind vane, and rain gauge.

451755.title: Mountain Weather
451755.description: Mountains provide some unique weather, and are often difficult places for forecasters to predict the weather. This category is about weather you'd likely find in the mountains.

links.title: MountainWeather.com
links.description: Contains weather information for Jackson Hole, Wyoming, USA and the Teton Mountains. Radar images and forecasts.

links.title: Mountain Weather Information Service
links.description: Contains forecasts for areas of the United Kingdom. Available as PDF files.

links.title: NOVA: Volcano Above the Clouds
links.description: Find out how mountains create their own distinct weather patterns, often causing wet weather on one side and a dry, clear climate on the other.

451756.title: Chinook Wind
451756.description: A Chinook wind occurs when a strong wind is forced down the side of a mountain, causing it to compress and warm. These winds can reach very high speeds, and can warm the air temperature by a large amount in a short time.

links.title: Wikipedia: Chinook Wind
links.description: Details chinooks in Alberta, and talks about how they occur.

links.title: MadSci Network
links.description: Explains why rain falls in drops rather than a stream like from the bath faucet.

links.title: MadSci Network
links.description: Contains a description of why rain seems to come all at once, and how rain forms.

links.title: What's the Chance of Rain ?
links.description: Printible worksheet coupled with an interative lesson. Investigates the chances of getting low, normal or high rainfall during an El Niño year in Australia.

links.title: Does It Rain More Often on Weekends?
links.description: Scientific study shows where it's more likely to rain on the weekends in the United States.

links.title: Rainbows
links.description: Gives an explanation of rainbows and how they occur.

links.title: What is a Rainbow?
links.description: Where older students can learn about "one of the most spectacular light shows observed on earth."

links.title: Weather Photography
links.description: Many photographs of colourful rainbows from the Australian Severe Weather Photography collection.

links.title: Circles of Light: The Mathematics of Rainbows
links.description: Explains reflection, refraction, and how together they make a rainbow.

links.title: NWS Winter Safety
links.description: Lists information about how to handle winter weather situations.

links.title: The Four Seasons
links.description: Includes games, coloring pages, crafts, and stationery for each of the four seasons. From PrimaryGames.com

links.title: The Electronic Passport to Seasons
links.description: A basic description of seasons with a diagram.

links.title: Winter Storms
links.description: Try out Scholastic's Interactive Weather Maker and learn how the wind chill factor works.

links.title: Snow Crystals
links.description: A complete guide to the science of snow crystals. Find out who did the first systematic study in 1954 and how such beautiful, symmetric shapes are formed.

links.title: All About Snow
links.description: Answers to questions about snow. Features snow facts, a snow glossary, and a snow gallery.

links.title: Ice and Snow
links.description: Learn about ice and snow from researchers in Antarctica.

links.title: National Snow and Ice Data Center
links.description: A resource for data and information about all forms of snow and ice.

451751.title: Lake Effect Snow
451751.description: Lake effect snow is caused by cool air crossing a warm lake, where it is warmed and picks up extra moisture. On the other side of the lake, the air is cooled and it deposits the moisture on the land in the form of snow.

links.title: Lake-Effect Snow Forecasting
links.description: Goes into detail about how forecasters are trying to better predict lake effect snow.

links.title: Lake-Effect Snow
links.description: Teaches what lake effect snow is with easy to understand diagrams.

links.title: Wikipedia: Lake Effect Snow
links.description: Contains a description of lake effect snow with diagram and satellite image.

links.title: The Lake Effect Snow
links.description: Michael Champion's fifth grade class in Onekama, Michigan created a presentation about the lake effect snow.

links.title: Straight Dope: What's the Physics Behind "Lake Effect Snow"?
links.description: Describes what lake effect snow is, from a physics point of view.

451727.title: Wind
451727.description: This category is for sites that describe the wind. Wind is the movement of air in the atmosphere.

links.title: What Is Wind?
links.description: Explains what wind is, and gives the fastest wind speed ever recorded.

links.title: FAQ Air Chemistry and Physics
links.description: Answers question about the air, gases, the wind, and pressure.

links.title: Australian Government - Bureau of Meteorology
links.description: Instructions for students how to measure wind speed with minimal equipment and surprising accuracy.

links.title: Where Does the Wind Come From?
links.description: Explains how differences in air pressure can cause the wind.

links.title: Weather Whiz Kids: Wind
links.description: Explain the jet stream, global wind patterns, plus land and sea breezes.

links.title: Forces and Winds: Online Meteorology Guide
links.description: Describes in detail what causes wind, the different kinds of wind, and the friction the Earth causes.

links.title: Tornado Facts For Kids
links.description: Facts on tornados; a powerful tube of spinning air that touches the ground.

links.title: Tropical Cyclone Facts For Kids
links.description: Facts on tropical cyclone; a huge spinning storm that forms over warm ocean waters near the Earth's Equator.

451729.title: Jet Stream
451729.description: A jet stream is a narrow band of fast moving air that is found high in the atmosphere.

links.title: Frequently Asked Questions About The Jet Stream
links.description: Includes how high the jet stream is, how fast it's moving, and how it affects weather.

links.title: Wikipedia: Jet Stream
links.description: Briefly explains the jet stream, and how they are important to airplanes.

links.title: NOVA Online: Inside the Jet Stream
links.description: Contains frequently asked questions, and answers what generates the jet stream.

links.title: Ridding the Jet Stream
links.description: Tells how some hot air balloonists have tried to ride the jet stream around the world, and how the location of the jet stream is used to help predict temperature.

links.title: Jet Stream: Current of Rapidly Moving Air
links.description: Explains how the jet stream forms between hot and cold air masses.

451730.title: Sirocco
451730.description: Sirocco is a strong southerly to southeasterly wind in the Mediterranean that originates from the Sahara and similar North African regions. It is aslo known locally as the qibli, scirocco, and jugo.

links.title: Wikipedia: Sirocco
links.description: Description of this Mediterranean strong wind.

450612.title: Social Studies
450612.description: This category lists sites that deal with the way people work and live in communities.       Sites geared toward social studies teachers will not be listed here.

links.title: Social Studies for Kids
links.description: Offers articles, links, and fun facts, on history, geography, cultures, holidays, economics, and archaeology.

links.title: PBS - GlobalTribe
links.description: TV series, combining the spirit of travel with exploring global issues, finds the unsung heroes on the forefront of change.

links.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica Students
links.description: Browse categories and articles related to social studies, along with a world atlas, timelines and Spotlight Archive.

links.title: MrDowling.com
links.description: Browse through topics from prehistory through conflicts in the Middle East.  Includes FAQs, standard-based lesson plans, assignments, interactive quizzes, and audio files.

links.title: Toporopa
links.description: Provides quizzes about geography, history, flags, metropolitan areas and capitals of European countries.

links.title: World Geography Games
links.description: Offers learning games to test geography knowledge including continents, oceans, Earth, atmosphere, waters, mountains, US states and all the countries of the world.

450782.title: Archaeology
450782.description: This category lists pages and sites about archaeology, the scientific study the fossil relics, tools, and monuments left by ancient peoples. By examining artifacts, archaeologists are able to gain an understanding of ancient cultures and civilizations.

links.title: NOVA Online: Lost City of Arabia
links.description: Join a team of archaeologists as they search for Ubar, the lost city of Arabia, and see how they apply the technology of remote sensing to "see" the site without actually excavating it.

links.title: North Ferriby Bronze Age Boats
links.description: Information on the three bronze age boats found by the River Humber at North Ferriby

links.title: Mysterious Places
links.description: Mali, Easter Island, Stonehenge, Chichen Itza, and other ancient civilizations and sacred sites.

links.title: Colonial Williamsburg: Archaeology Collections & Lab
links.description: Simple look at what archaeology is and how it enhances the study of history. Includes games and projects kids can do at home.

links.title: Iron Age Celts
links.description: Learn about the people who lived in Britain 2000 years ago.  From the BBC.

links.title: Unlocking the Past
links.description: Talks about cultures in contact and conflict, new lands and environments, building cities, and archeology of work.

links.title: Mummy Bear
links.description: Trace Mummy Bear's history to learn about the process of mummification.

links.title: Simon Fraser University Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology - Young Adventurers' Page
links.description: Provides a look at virtual museum exhibits, land of archaeology, building the temples, also with fun, and games.

links.title: NOVA Online: The Takla Makan Mummies
links.description: Features illustrated details of these 3000-year-old bodies found in a remote Chinese desert.

links.title: Bodies of the Bogs
links.description: An illustrated feature from Archaeology on the remains of many hundreds of people which have come to light during peat cutting in northwestern Europe.

links.title: Ice Mummies
links.description: Archaeological expedition in search of frozen sacrifices on the summit of Sara Sara in Peru.

links.title: NOVA Online: Mummies 101
links.description: Photographs and descriptions of remains found in Europe, China, Egypt and South America. Includes an explanation of both intentional and accidental mummification.

450785.title: Egyptian
450785.description: Mummification was used in Ancient Egypt to preserve the dead, and they believed it would assist their journey into the afterlife.

links.title: Experiment: Make a Fruit Mummy
links.description: Illustrated step by step instructions for drying out a slice of apple using the same process used to preserve the dead in Ancient Egypt.

links.title: The Royal Theban Mummy Project
links.description: Presents archeological data about New Kingdom and Third Intermediate Period royal mummies from the Theban cache tombs in an accessible way.

links.title: BBC News: Ancient Egyptian animal cemetery found
links.description: Describes the discovery of the mummified remains of falcons and rodents dating from 300 BC.

links.title: Ti Ameny Net
links.description: An ancient Egyptian mummy displayed at the Ancient World Gallery. Includes CT scans, x-rays, and analyses.

links.title: Royal Ontario Museum: Mummies, mummies, mummies!
links.description: Has photographs and decorations to download for painting, and a procedure for a mummification experiment.

links.title: Smithsonian: Egyptian Mummification
links.description: Provides explanations about how and why it was done, the ceremonies that were performed, and what sorts of things were included with the body.

450784.title: Inca
450784.description: This ancient civilization in South America had a tradition of mummifying dead bodies.

451136.title: Cultures
451136.description: This category lists sites that introduce young people to the cultures found throughout the world. It includes sites about the beliefs, values, lifestyles, and skills of various people groups.

links.title: Cultures
links.description: Devoted to cultures, living and ancient, and the promotion of world communication. Includes photos, drawings, animations, sounds, links to encyclopedias.

links.title: Kulture Kids
links.description: Features multicultural recipes, crafts, and activities. Non-profit organization behind the site also promotes cultural appreciation through arts education, workshops, and theater.

links.title: Mountain Voices
links.description: Presents interviews with over 300 people who live in mountain and highland regions round the world. Their testimonies offer a personal perspective on change and development.

links.title: Online Exhibits
links.description: Includes previews of history records, thoughts, and events.

links.title: Multicultural Education through Miniatures
links.description: Has pictures and stories of dolls, puppets, and small figures from many countries. Use photos, stories, activities, and games in school projects.

links.title: Odyssey Online
links.description: A journey to explore Near Eastern, Egyptian, Greek, Roman, and sub-Saharan African cultures. Make your own discoveries through cool puzzles, games, and worksheets.

links.title: Mama Lisa's World of Children and International Culture
links.description: Children's songs, nursery rhymes and poetry from all over the globe presented both in English and their native languages. Many include MP3, realaudio or midi sound clips and sheet music. [English, French, Spanish]

links.title: Countries and Their Cultures
links.description: Detailed, illustrated articles on more than one hundred world cultures.

links.title: Pulse of the Planet
links.description: Two-minute glimpses, complete with sound clips, into the cultures of the worlds. See and hear how people live, work, and play. From National Science Foundation.

links.title: National Geographic - Travel & Cultures
links.description: Includes photos, maps, videos, flags and facts, all indexed by continent and country.

451137.title: Clothing
451137.description: A collection of sites about clothing in different places and time periods. This category includes the history of clothing.

links.title: ThoughtCo.: The History of Clothing
links.description: Who invented the bikini, tuxedo, shoes, and other articles of clothing.

links.title: Civilization.ca - Marius Barbeau - Clothing
links.description: Some clothing from the Canadian Museum of Civilization. A glimpse of Canadian culture from 1883-1969.

450771.title: Economics
450771.description: Sites in this category are constructed for, and teach, children and teenagers about money, banking and investing, saving, budgeting, borrowing, and other basic economic activities and institutions.

links.title: Washingtonpost.com: Business Glossary
links.description: Searchable dictionary of more than 1,250 business terms.

links.title: Taxnotes: History Project
links.description: Information about the history of American taxation, with web-based documentary publications and original research.

links.title: Museum of American Finance
links.description: Online exhibits and resources chronicling the role of finance and capital markets in American history.

links.title: Taxnotes: Tax History Museum
links.description: An interactive overview of the history of American revenue policy and politics, with narrative text and multimedia material.

links.title: IRS Tax Information for Students
links.description: Educates teenagers about the U.S. tax system, the effect of taxes on their day-to-day lives, and new electronic ways to file tax returns.

links.title: Globalization Facts For Kids
links.description: Globalization is about how countries and people around the world become more connected and similar. It touches on many parts of life, like how we buy and sell things (economics), how we use new tools (technology), how countries work together (politics), and even what we wear or watch (culture).

450772.title: Money
450772.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help young people learn about money. It includes information on making money, spending it and investing it.

links.title: FDIC: Learning Bank
links.description: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation is the US governmental agency that insures bank depositors if their bank fails. This site is designed to help kids know how this agency works and why it is important to have.

links.title: PBS: Electric Money
links.description: Explores how computers have revolutionized the financial world.

links.title: Dollars and Sense for Kids
links.description: A guide to banking, history of money, fun facts, games, and riddles.

links.title: Practical Money Skills Games
links.description: Games and simulations to learn about spending, saving, investing and credit cards.

links.title: Kids' Money For Kids
links.description: Features making money, allowances, spending, saving and investing.

450773.title: Calculators and Converters
450773.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help young people figure changes in the value of money. It includes loan calculators, investment calculators and currency converters.

links.title: Savings Calculator
links.description: Shows how much money you need to save every day, week, and month to reach a long-term savings goal.

links.title: XE Currency Converter
links.description: Online conversion for national currencies, special units and precious metals.

450777.title: Currency
450777.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help kids and teens learn more about currency, including what it is how it works, and what different currencies look like.

links.title: Change Maker
links.description: An educational game where the player must calculate the change given for a money purchase. Currencies from the United States, Canada, Australia, United Kingdom, and Mexico are available.

links.title: Counterfeit Detection
links.description: Simple guide to determining whether various types of U.S. currency are real or fake.

links.title: History and Photo Catalog of World Paper Money
links.description: Contains images of old and recent world paper money listed by countries. Discover nature and history of the world currency through the designs and graphics.

450778.title: Canada
450778.description: For sites that focus on Canadian currency.

links.title: Currency Museum of the Bank of Canada
links.description: Explores the evolution and history of money throughout the world. In English and French.

links.title: Royal Canadian Mint
links.description: Official site of the agency which produces Canada's money. In English and French.

450779.title: United States
450779.description: This category is for sites which focus on US currency.

links.title: The U.S. Mint's Site for Kids
links.description: The awesome history of coins and how the mint makes money. Interactive clubhouse for kids and teachers includes cartoons, history, and news.

links.title: NOVA Online: Secrets of Making Money
links.description: Takes a look at the new U.S. currency, with interactive exploration of both new and old features.

links.title: American Currency Exhibit
links.description: This online exhibit of U.S. money presents the history as well as photographs of past and present bank notes.

links.title: America's Historic Currency Exhibit
links.description: An educational exhibit which uses American currency to chronicle some of history's greatest secrets. The site includes currency printed by Benjamin Franklin. Also includes an example of the money found on the body of Abraham Lincoln at the time of his death.

links.title: The MegaPenny Project
links.description: Find out what a thousand pennies, a million, or even one trillion would look like, how much they would weigh, what they would be worth, and how far they could reach.

450775.title: Earning
450775.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help children and teenagers learn how to earn money.

links.title: Young and Successful
links.description: Supports the needs of young people from around the world as they attempt to build and thrive in both their personal and professional lives.

450774.title: Saving and Investing
450774.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help children and teenagers learn how to invest money. It includes information on stocks, bonds, and mutual funds.

450776.title: Spending
450776.description: This category lists pages and sites designed to help young people learn to spend money responsibly.

450780.title: Organizations
450780.description: This category lists the sites of organizations which help children and teenagers learn more about economics.

links.title: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA)
links.description: Non-profit educational association of students preparing for careers in business; links businesspeople, parents, and junior high and high school students in local chapters.

links.title: Young Americans Center for Financial Education
links.description: Programs are designed to provide children with knowledge about the free enterprise system. It includes online tutorials as well as information about summer camp and other programs.

450786.title: Geography
450786.description:
Geography is the study of earth and its features.

This category lists sites that provide information or educational activities related to geography for children and teenagers.

links.title: ThoughtCo.: Geography
links.description: Features articles, fact sheets, and maps to explore landscapes, peoples, places, and environments both near and far.

links.title: The British Museum: Middle East and Asia
links.description: Explore the area through objects which chart the cultures from prehistory to the present day.

links.title: Geographia
links.description: Provides information about the people, history, culture, natural terrain, and tourist attractions in Asia, Africa, Europe, Latin America, and the Caribbean.

links.title: World Monuments Map Puzzle
links.description: Interactive puzzle for locations and significance of the cultural monuments of the world.  Also printable map of continents.  Requires Windows  95,  98 or 3.1.

links.title: City Population
links.description: Statistics and maps about the major population clusters of the world. Also information about the capitals and principal cities of many countries.  In English and German.

links.title: Great Circle Calculator
links.description: Features calculating direct line distances between any two points on the earth's globe.

links.title: Countries of the World
links.description: Cultural and geographical information about countries of the world through interactive maps.

links.title: World Trivia Web Quizzes
links.description: Learn fascinating facts about world countries. Each quiz selects 10 world trivia facts at random from a total set of 480.

links.title: Atlantic Ocean
links.description: Provides facts about the second largest ocean including background, geography, economic significance, transportation.

links.title: Climate Zone.com
links.description: Directory of world climates organized by continents, regions, US states/areas. Has the world map, and alphabetical country list.

links.title: The Greatest Places
links.description: Explore seven of the most geographically dynamic locations on Earth. Learn about the Imax film, add your own favorite place, get a Greatest Places image, or check out the question of the week.

links.title: Sheppard Software - Geography Games
links.description: Offers games which test geography of the world. Country names are spoken and brief descriptions are provided.

links.title: World in the Balance
links.description: Based on the NOVA educational TV program.  Articles cover topics such as human consumption, sustainable population rate, and the impact of the average age within a country.   Page includes people counter, photos, quizzes, and maps.

links.title: BBC Landscapes of Scotland
links.description: Develop map skills while exploring the highlands, central lowlands and islands of Scotland.

links.title: CIA The World Factbook
links.description: Features map and brief descriptions of the geography, people, government, economy, communications, transportation, military and transnational issues.

links.title: Photo Diaries and Sketches
links.description: View photos taken from around the world during Robert Bremec's travels. Includes slideshow feature.

links.title: Enchanted Learning - Geography
links.description: Collection of geography pages, printouts and activities for students.

links.title: Library of Congress - Country Studies
links.description: Find in-depth information about everything from geography to weather, from government to religion, for more than 100 countries. Prepared by the Federal Research Division of the Library of Congress.

links.title: Great Circle Mapper
links.description: Displays maps and computes distances along a geodesic path. Includes a searchable database of airports and other locations.

links.title: Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names
links.description: Searchable database of place names around the world tells where it is located.  Includes more than a million ancient and contemporary names including variations.

links.title: Test your Geography Knowledge
links.description: Contains quizzes on maps of continents, countries, and states.

links.title: Euratlas: Physical atlas
links.description: Interactive map of Europe locating mountains, rivers, countries, and towns. Includes a map with links to photographs of the featured locations.

links.title: National Geographic - Education GeoBee
links.description: Online game changes every day with ten new geography questions.

links.title: Kiddle: Atlantic Ocean facts for kids
links.description: Provides comprehensive facts about the Atlantic Ocean's size, depth, bathymetry, water characteristics, ocean currents (gyres), major seas, and historical context. Features clear data tables and explanations of key oceanographic features such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

links.title: Black Sea Facts For Kids
links.description: The Black Sea is a large sea located in Eurasia, between Europe, the Caucasus mountains, and Anatolia. Many important rivers flow into it, such as the Don, Danube, and Dnieper.

links.title: Caspian Sea Facts For Kids
links.description: The Caspian Sea is the biggest inland body of water on Earth. It's so large that people sometimes call it the world's largest lake, and sometimes a full sea.

links.title: Indian Ocean Facts For Kids
links.description: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean on Earth. It covers about 70,560,000 square kilometers.

links.title: Mediterranean Sea Facts For Kids
links.description: The Mediterranean Sea is a large body of water that separates three continents: Europe to the north, Africa to the south, and Asia to the east. It's almost completely surrounded by land.

links.title: Pacific Ocean Facts For Kids
links.description: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean on Earth. It stretches between Asia and Australia on its western side, and the Americas on its eastern side.

links.title: Southern Ocean Facts For Kids
links.description: The Southern Ocean is the ocean that surrounds Antarctica. It was officially recognized as a separate ocean in 2000.

links.title: Countries of the World
links.description: This blog contains lists of all the countries of the world (recognized by UN) along with their flags, maps, national anthems, geographical summary data and other useful information. It also publishes news and facts from all over the world.

450929.title: Africa
450929.description: This category lists sites that introduce young people to the cultures found throughout Africa. It includes sites about the beliefs, values, lifestyles, and skills of various people groups.

links.title: PBS Kids' Africa
links.description: Journey with Anansi the spider as he explores Africa's amazing places, its civilizations, and its cultures.

links.title: Geographia - Africa
links.description: Introduces the different countries of Africa and their people.

links.title: Wikipedia - Africa
links.description: Offers article on history, geography, government, economy, people, transportation, culture, language and education.

links.title: The Africa Guide - African People & Culture
links.description: Provides visitor information along with background material on the people and culture including their music, cuisine, festivals, arts and crafts.

links.title: Sheppard Software - All About Africa
links.description: Develop a mental map of Africa, its countries, capitals and geography through playing interactive games.

links.title: PBS - Wonders of the African World
links.description: Documentary by Henry Louis Gates, Jr. about African history and culture. Includes audio, classroom activities and additional resources.

links.title: African Studies Center
links.description: Guide to assist K-12 teachers, librarians, and students in locating on-line resources on Africa that can be used in the classroom, for research and studies.

links.title: Congo River Facts For Kids
links.description: The Congo River is a huge river in Africa. It is also known as the Zaire River.

links.title: Lake Tanganyika Facts For Kids
links.description: Lake Tanganyika is a huge lake located in the Great Rift Valley of central Africa. It's like a giant, long ribbon of water.

links.title: Lake Victoria Facts For Kids
links.description: Lake Victoria, also called Victoria Nyanza, is a huge lake in Africa. It is also known by local names like Ukerewe and Nnalubaale.

links.title: Niger River Facts For Kids
links.description: The Niger River is a super important river in West Africa. It's more than 4,180 kilometers long.

links.title: Nile Facts For Kids
links.description: The Nile is a very important river in northeastern Africa. It flows north and empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

links.title: Sahara Facts For Kids
links.description: The Sahara is a huge desert in North Africa. It is one of the largest deserts on Earth.

450965.title: Algeria
450965.description: Algeria culture for kids and teens

links.title: US Library of Congress - Country Study: Algeria
links.description: December 1993 report on the country's profile, history, geography, economy, government, politics and national security.

links.title: Fact Monster - Algeria
links.description: Fast facts and information for kids about the country's geography, government, history, economy, land and people.

links.title: allAfrica.com - Algeria
links.description: News reports and headlines from African and worldwide sources, updated with breaking news.

links.title: Perry-Castañeda Library Map Collection - Algeria Maps
links.description: Country, city and thematic maps, along with links to maps on other web sites. From the Perry-Castañeda Library Map Collection at the University of Texas.

links.title: Lonely Planet - Algeria
links.description: Facts and advice for traveling along with background material on the culture and history of the country.

links.title: BBC News - Country Profile: Algeria
links.description: Provides overview, key facts and events, timelines and leader profiles along with current news.

links.title: Embassy of Algeria to the United States of America
links.description: Official site provides news, information and photos about the country and its culture, tourism, trade and foreign affairs along with consular services. [English, French]

450967.title: Angola
450967.description: This category lists sites that introduce young people to the cultures found throughout Angola. It includes sites about the beliefs, values, lifestyles, and skills of various people groups.

links.title: Five Star Flags - Angola
links.description: View the current flag, its colors, and read the history behind the previous flags.

links.title: US Library of Congress - Country Study: Angola

450877.title: North Macedonia
450877.description:
North Macedonia, known as Macedonia before February 2019, and officially the Republic of North Macedonia, is a country in Southeast Europe.

It gained independence in 1991 as one of the successor states of Yugoslavia.

It is a landlocked country bordering Kosovo[e] to the northwest, Serbia to the north, Bulgaria to the east, Greece to the south, and Albania to the west.

It constitutes approximately the northern third of the larger geographical region of Macedonia.

Skopje, the capital and largest city, is home to a quarter of the country's 1.83 million people.

from Wikipedia

450920.title: Syria
450920.description:
Syria (Arabic: سُورِيَا or سُورِيَة), officially the Syrian Arab Republic (Arabic: الجمهورية العربية السورية), is a Western Asian country located in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Levant.

It is a unitary republic that consists of 14 governorates (subdivisions), and is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the west, Turkey to the north, Iraq to the east and southeast, Jordan to the south, and Israel and Lebanon to the southwest. Cyprus lies to the west across the Mediterranean Sea.

links.title: EyeWitness:  History Through The Eyes Of Those Who Lived It

links.title: Tamerlane Facts For Kids
links.description: Tamerlane (born April 8, 1336 – died February 18, 1405) was a powerful Turkic leader and conqueror. He lived in the 14th century.

450672.title: Africa

links.title: African History
links.description: Site created for middle school students spans the period from the Nok to Nelson Mandela. Includes facts in brief as well as a more detailed look at some of the major people and events of the era.

links.title: Apartheid Facts For Kids
links.description: Apartheid was a system of unfair rules in South Africa. It was in place from 1948 until the early 1990s.

450656.title: Asia
450656.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about this history of Asia.

links.title: Mesopotamia Facts For Kids
links.description: Mesopotamia (which means "land between rivers" in Greek) is a historic area in Western Asia.

links.title: Ashoka the Great Facts For Kids
links.description: Ashoka (or Asoka) was a great emperor of India. He ruled the Maurya Empire from about 268 BCE to 232 BCE.

links.title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk Facts For Kids
links.description: Kemal Atatürk (also known as Mustafa Kemal Atatürk) was a very important Turkish statesman and military leader. He was the first President of Turkey from 1923 until he passed away in 1938.

links.title: Cyrus the Great Facts For Kids

links.title: Jawaharlal Nehru Facts For Kids

links.title: Suleiman the Magnificent Facts For Kids
links.description: Suleiman I (born November 6, 1494 – died September 6, 1566) was the tenth and longest-reigning Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. In the West, he is known as Suleiman the Magnificent.

450657.title: China
450657.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about the history of China.

links.title: Electronic Passport to Chinese History

links.title: History of China

links.title: History of Chinese Invention and Discovery
links.description: A timeline of historical events features scientific and everyday inventions, and compares the time of discovery with when it happened in Western civilization.

links.title: Condensed China: Chinese History for Beginners

links.title: A Visual Sourcebook of Chinese Civilization

links.title: History of China

links.title: Ming Dynasty Facts For Kids
links.description: The Ming dynasty was a powerful family of emperors who ruled China from 1368 to 1644.

links.title: Tang Dynasty Facts For Kids
links.description: The Tang Dynasty was a very important time in Chinese history. It lasted from June 18, 618, to June 4, 907.

links.title: The American Experience - Nixon's China Game

links.title: Cultural Revolution Facts For Kids
links.description: The Cultural Revolution was a big change in China that lasted from 1966 to 1976. It was started by Mao Zedong, who was the leader of the Communist Party of China.

links.title: Mao Zedong Facts For Kids
links.description: Mao Zedong (born December 26, 1893 – died September 9, 1976), also known as Chairman Mao, was a Chinese leader, thinker, and military planner. He was a communist revolutionary who founded the People's Republic of China (PRC).

links.title: Sun Yat-sen Facts For Kids
links.description: Sun Yat-sen (also known by many other names; 12 November 1866 – 12 March 1925) was a Chinese statesman and doctor. He is famous for being the first provisional president of the Republic of China.

1024723.title: Japan
1024723.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about the history of Japan.

links.title: Kids Web Japan: Explore Japan

links.title: Japan Mint: History of Japanese Coins
links.description: Learn about the history of Japanese coins through time.

links.title: Japan Center for Asian Historical Records
links.description: Provides electronic access to digital images of historical records about modern Japan-Asia relations held by Japanese national institutions.

links.title: Meiji Restoration Facts For Kids
links.description: The Meiji Restoration was a major political event in Japan. It happened in 1868 and brought back the power of the Emperor of Japan.

450658.title: Europe
450658.description: This category lists pages and sites that deal with the history of Europe.

links.title: Euratlas
links.description: Maps showing the history of Europe as a whole.  Photographs of modern Europe and of European artifacts.

links.title: Peter the Great Facts For Kids
links.description: Peter I (June 9, 1672 – February 8, 1725), often called Peter the Great, was a powerful Russian ruler. He led the Tsardom of Russia from 1682 and later the Russian Empire until his death in 1725.

links.title: Joseph Stalin Facts For Kids
links.description: Joseph Stalin (born Iosif Vissarionovich Stalin; 18 December 1878 – 5 March 1953) was the powerful leader of the Soviet Union from 1922 until his death. He took over from Vladimir Lenin as the country's leader.

450665.title: Austria

450669.title: France

links.title: Eiffel Tower

links.title: French Revolution Facts For Kids

links.title: Napoleon Facts For Kids
links.description: Napoleon Bonaparte (born August 15, 1769 – died May 5, 1821) was a famous French military and political leader. He was known as Napoleon I when he became "Emperor of the French.

450668.title: Germany
450668.description: This category lists pages and sites about the history of Germany.

links.title: German Encyclopedia: 1900-45

links.title: The Rise of Adolf Hitler

links.title: German History
links.description: Features early, medieval and modern history.

links.title: Otto von Bismarck Facts For Kids
links.description: Otto von Bismarck (born Otto Eduard Leopold von Bismarck, April 1, 1815 – July 30, 1898) was a very important German leader. He was a statesman and diplomat from Prussia.

450664.title: Italy
450664.description: This category is for sites about the history of Italy.

450667.title: Reformation

links.title: The Life and Times of Queen Elizabeth I

links.title: Mr Dowling - The Renaissance.

links.title: Elizabethan Costumes

links.title: La Renaissance
links.description: This virtual art museum covers the era its artists from Italy, The Netherlands, Germany and France.

links.title: Onboard the Mary Rose
links.description: This site takes us on a tour of Henry VIII's favorite boat.

450659.title: United Kingdom
450659.description: This category lists pages and sites relating to the history of the United Kingdom (U.K.). The United Kingdom includes Northern Ireland, Scotland, England, and Wales.

links.title: Encyclopaedia of British History

links.title: Smuggler's Britain

links.title: The Black Death
links.description: Information on the spread, the effects, the medical response and the final impact the disease had on England in 1348-1349.

links.title: The Domesday Book Online

Commissioned in December 1085 by William the Conqueror. Also includes information on how it was compiled, who contributed to writing it and life in the 11th century.

links.title: The Oliver Cromwell Website
links.description: Provides in-depth information about his life from 1599 to 1658. Features a time-line, a biography, FAQs, quotes and suggested further reading. Includes illustrations and photos.

links.title: Regia Anglorum - Anglo-Saxon and Viking Britain
links.description: Offers a complete overview of life within this period. Includes sections on history, weapons and warfare, everyday life and religion as well as stories and poems of the time.

links.title: The Growth of Women's Rights - 1800 to 1900
links.description: A simple time-line detailing legislation passed within the century. Also gives information on the emergence of the first woman doctor, the beginnings of the suffragette movement and an employment table showing women in various professions during 1900.

Focuses on the early history and aims of the founder Millicent Fawcett, a section on the Pankhursts as well as detailing the various methods used by the group to highlight their issues. links.title: The National Archives - Treasures
links.description: Covers aspects of British history from domesday to the present day and is part of the National Grid for Learning. Provided by the UK Public Records Office.

links.title: BBC - KS2 History
links.description: Interactive information on British and world history, famous people, and historical skills.

links.title: BBC - The Anglo-Saxons

links.title: Learning Curve - The Great War 1914 - 1918
links.description: An online exhibition on the First World War. Includes information, video clips, photographs and maps taken from the archives and also provides worksheets for young students.

links.title: The Workhouse

links.title: The Battle of Britain

links.title: British Empire Facts For Kids

links.title: Industrial Revolution Facts For Kids
links.description: The Industrial Revolution was a time in history when the way things were made changed a lot and very quickly. Before this, most products were made by hand in small workshops.

450660.title: England
450660.description: This category lists pages and sites relating to the history of England.

links.title: Berkshire History for Kids -  Civil War Chaos
links.description: Recounts the story of King Charles I and the events leading up to his execution. Provides links to places of interest in Berkshire.

links.title: Chronology of Events in the History of English
links.description: Concise list of key events specifically referring to the language and its evolvement. Covers the Pre-English, Anglo-Saxon, Middle and Modern periods.

links.title: The Blitz
links.description: Summary of the bombings which occurred in London during the second World War. Also provides links to photographs of the events and further reading.

links.title: The Peterloo Massacre
links.description: Offers information on the events of 16th August 1819 when a meeting of 60,000 protesters gathered to demand the reform of parliament. Fearing revolution the magistrates present ordered dispersement and the military rode into the crowd killing many.

links.title: An Island Story - A History of England for Boys and Girls

450663.title: Northern Ireland
450663.description: This category lists pages and sites relating to the history of Northern Ireland.

links.title: History of Derry
links.description: A concise history of the city from the 6th century AD until 1921.

Offers interactive presentations on King William III, the plantation of Scottish/English settlers in the 17th century, the Easter Rising, the 'Troubles' and the Good Friday Agreement. Includes illustrations, photos and further reading in each section.

links.title: Timelines - Northern Ireland

450662.title: Scotland

links.title: Before the Clearances - 17th and 18th Century Scottish Costume

450671.title: Yugoslavia
450671.description: Yugoslavia was first formed as a kingdom in 1918. It was a monarchy formed as the "Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes" after World War I. The six countries that were once part of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia are Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, and Slovenia. It fell during World War II.   It was  recreated as a Socialist state in 1945 after World War II. It disintegrated in the Yugoslav Wars  during the 1990s.  The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was created in 1992. It was a federation on the territory of the republics of Serbia (including the autonomous provinces of Vojvodina, Kosovo and Metohija) and Montenegro.  It was reformed as The Union of Serbia and Montenegro on February 4, 2003. This was a weaker union of the nations.  In 2006 Serbia and Montenegro each declared their independence from the union. Yugoslavia no longer exists.

links.title: BBC News: Timeline: Break-up of Yugoslavia
