links.description: A series of web pages on the history and culture of ancient Rome.

links.title: On Roman Numerals
links.description: Check out the roman numeral converter.

links.title: Echoes from the Ancients
links.description: Highlights an archaeological dig at a site where Jewish men, women and children held off trained Roman forces for 47 days. From PBS.

links.title: The Roman Empire in the First Century
links.description: Brief look at the empire itself, ancient voices, social order, and daily life. From PBS.

links.title: Rome Project
links.description: Clickable maps of the Roman Empire, plus information on politics, people, and places.

links.title: BBC: KS2: Roman Empire
links.description: Presents the people and lifestyles of the Roman Empire; army life, invasions, rebellions, leisure, family, religion, and games.

links.title: Roman Empire Facts For Kids
links.description: The Roman Empire was one of the biggest and most powerful empires in the ancient world.

links.title: Augustus Facts For Kids
links.description: Augustus (born Gaius Octavius, later known as Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus) was the first and one of the most important Roman Emperors. He lived from 63 BC to 14 AD.

links.title: Julius Caesar Facts For Kids
links.description: Gaius Julius Caesar (born around July 100 BC – died March 15, 44 BC) was a very important military leader, politician, and writer in ancient Rome. He lived at the end of the Roman Republic.

links.title: Constantine the Great Facts For Kids
links.description: Constantine I (born February 27, 272 AD – died May 22, 337 AD) was a very powerful general who became an emperor of the Roman Empire. He ruled until his death.

450646.title: Eighteenth Century
450646.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about historical events in the 18th century.

links.title: Royal Proclamation of 1763
links.description: The declaration by the King of England that set the boundaries of lands in North America for settlement by colonists and set apart that land that was held by the Indian nations. Additions include headings, introduction, and a map.

links.title: From Revolution to Reconstruction: Documents: Paristreaty 1763
links.description: The actual text of the treaty.

links.title: Age of Enlightenment Facts For Kids
links.description: The Age of Enlightenment was a big cultural movement in Europe during the 18th century.

450647.title: Industrial Revolution
450647.description: Beginning around 1750 AD in England, this rapid growth of industry rapidly expanded to America. Although this growth spurt is still continuing, this period of history falls between 1750 AD and the early 1900's.

links.title: Inside an American factory
links.description: The year is 1904. See inside an American factory via film clips.

450625.title: Middle Ages
450625.description: These are the "middle" centuries, from approximately 600 AD to 1500 AD.

links.title: Build a Medieval Castle
links.description: Freeware.  Requires Windows  95,  98 or 3.1.

links.title: The Medieval World
links.description: Collection of illustrated articles cover aspects of British history from 1066-1500. From Spartacus Internet Encyclopaedia.

links.title: The Electronic Passport to the Middle Ages
links.description: Guide for middle school students introduces the period. Also provides in-depth information about specific topics such as feudalism, the Vikings, the Byzantine Empire, and the bubonic plague.

links.title: The Magna Carta
links.description: Translation from the Latin of the first version of the Magna Carta, signed by King John at Runnymede in 1215. Links to glossary and Latin original text.

links.title: History of the Incas
links.description: School project made for an eighth grade class provides a brief introduction to the civilization.

links.title: Shields, Knights and Heraldry
links.description: Freeware (free software) from Owl and Mouse suitable for classroom or home use.

links.title: Snayfwickby Castle
links.description: A tour of an imaginary castle and village with Lady Clare and Sir Claude. Created for first through third graders.

links.title: Castles for Kids
links.description: Links to sites that let kids learn how people in the middle ages lived, explore castles, and even build their own medieval creations.

links.title: Magna Carta:  Source of Civil Rights
links.description: Links to primary sources, including an original copy of England's famous document, learn why King John signed the charter and what rights he granted.

links.title: Abbasid Caliphate Facts For Kids
links.description: The Abbasid Caliphate was a powerful Muslim empire. It was the third major caliphate in Islamic history.

links.title: Aztecs Facts For Kids
links.description: The Aztecs were Native American people who lived in a region called Mesoamerica. They built a powerful empire that lasted from the 14th century to the 16th century.

links.title: Holy Roman Empire Facts For Kids
links.description: The Holy Roman Empire was a large group of lands in central Europe. These lands included many different regions and free cities.

links.title: Hundred Years' War Facts For Kids
links.description: The Hundred Years' War was a long conflict between France and England. It happened during the late Middle Ages, lasting 116 years from 1337 to 1453.

links.title: Middle Ages Facts For Kids
links.description: The Middle Ages was a long period in European history. It lasted for about a thousand years.

links.title: Mongol Empire Facts For Kids
links.description: The Mongol Empire was a huge area ruled by powerful Mongol leaders called Khans during the 1200s and 1300s.

links.title: Protestant Reformation Facts For Kids
links.description: The Protestant Reformation was a big series of changes that happened in the 16th century. It affected the Christian Church in Europe.

links.title: Thirty Years' War Facts For Kids
links.description: The Thirty Years' War was a long and terrible war that lasted from 1618 to 1648. Even though most of the fighting happened in Germany, many other powerful countries in Europe got involved.

links.title: Renaissance Facts For Kids
links.description: The Renaissance was a special time in European history. It started around the year 1400, right after the Middle Ages.

450626.title: Crusades
450626.description: This category is devoted to the Holy Wars fought between Christians and Muslims during the medieval period. It includes sites about wars fought between the Latin West and the Muslim East from the 11th to 14th centuries.

links.title: Catholic Encyclopedia: Crusades
links.description: Presents the Catholic perspective on the Crusades.

links.title: Crusades and Crusaders
links.description: An illustrated account of the main crusaders of the Middle Ages, including the Albigensian (Cathar) Crusade.

links.title: Crusades Facts For Kids
links.description: The Crusades were a series of religious wars. They were fought mainly between Christians from Europe and Muslims over control of the Holy Land.

450624.title: Nineteenth Century
450624.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about historical events in the 19th century.

links.title: 1876 Victorian England Revisited
links.description: Travel back in time to 1876 Victorian England and experience middle-class life as it was then.

links.title: Aspects of the Victorian Book
links.description: Learn about the changes in British printing technology during the 19th century. Includes illustrations, bindings and wood engraving; novels, penny dreadfuls, magazines and children's books.

links.title: The Age of Imperialism
links.description: Discusses United States expansionism around the turn of the century. Also provides basic information about international events in the same time period including the Boxer Rebellion and the Spanish-American War.

450648.title: Twentieth Century
450648.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about historical events in the 20th century.

links.title: Greatest Engineering Achievements of the 20th Century
links.description: Describes the twenty greatest engineering achievements as determined by the National Academy of Engineering.

links.title: Rpfuller.com: GCSE History Notes
links.description: GCSE revision notes, covering Germany, the Treaty of Versailles, interwar diplomacy, the causes of World War II, Russia, and the Cold War.

links.title: People's Century
links.description: History of the people, for the people, as told by the people who lived it. From PBS.

links.title: Historical Atlas of the 20th Century
links.description: Includes socio-economic trends, population and war statistics, and listings of world leaders.

links.title: Imperial War Museum
links.description: Tells the stories of how the wars of the twentieth century have affected people, covering all aspects of life in wartime. Includes online exhibitions.

links.title: Russian Revolution Facts For Kids
links.description: The Russian Revolution was a major event in Russia in 1917. It was a series of big changes that ended the rule of the Tsar (the emperor of Russia).

450652.title: World War I
450652.description: This category lists pages and sites about World War I. Also known as the Great War or the First World War, this war was waged from 1914-1918 between the Allies (Great Britain, France, Belgium, Russia, the United States, Italy, etc.) and the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, etc.). The war formally ended in 1919 with the signing of the Treaty of Versailles.

links.title: The Great War
links.description: Click through maps and images of Eastern Europe, follow an interactive timeline, or read historian interviews with this PBS companion site about World War I.

links.title: Encyclopedia of the First World War
links.description: Includes a timeline of the war, a look at the political and military leaders, an outline of major offensives, and statistics. Also provides information about weaponry, tactics, the arts of the period, and the role of women.

links.title: American Leaders Speak
links.description: Sound recordings of political speeches by American leaders during World War I and the presidential election of 1920.

links.title: The World War I Document Archive
links.description: Provides photographs, links, articles, a biographical dictionary and related resources.

links.title: Awesome Stories - The Lusitania
links.description: Presents an account of the German torpedo attack that sank the passenger liner and resulted in America's involvement in World War I.  Includes references to primary sources.  [Requires Macromedia Flash 5]

450649.title: World War II
450649.description: This category lists pages and sites about World War II, the most devastating war in human history. World War II began in 1939 as a European conflict. It grew into global conflict, however, pitting the Axis powers of Germany, Italy, and Japan against the Allied powers which included the United States and Great Britain. The bloody conflict drew to a close in 1945, with Italy surrendering on May 2, Germany on May 7, and Japan on Aug. 14.

links.title: Navajo Code Talkers
links.description: Tells the story of the Navajo volunteers who served in communications security roles in the Pacific Theater.

links.title: What Did You Do In The War, Grandma?
links.description: Oral histories of Rhode Island women during World War II, written by high school honors students.

links.title: Alternative Service in the Second World War: Conscientious Objectors in Canada 1939-1945.
links.description: Audio interviews, stories, photographs, and film footage tell the story about Canada's 10,000+ conscientious objectors.

links.title: EyeWitness To World War Two
links.description: Eyewitness accounts of soldiers and civilians.

links.title: World War II Posters:  Powers of Persuasion
links.description: An exhibit of World War II posters from the holdings of the National Archives and Records Administration.

links.title: Experiencing War : D-Day 60th Anniversary, June 6, 1944-2004
links.description: American veterans tell of their experiences during the war. Collected  for the Veterans History Project by the U.S. Library of Congress.

links.title: Awesome Stories - America In World War II: The Forgotten Posters
links.description: Government posters that capitalized on changed American attitudes following Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor and America's entry into WWII.

links.title: BBC: WW2 People's War
links.description: People share their experiences of the war. Includes accounts from both soldiers and those at home in the United Kingdom.

links.title: Tweedale's War
links.description: The beginning chapters of an R.A.F. signalman's personal memories of the War in the East.

links.title: Nazi Germany Facts For Kids
links.description: Nazi Germany describes the country of Germany between 1933 and 1945. During this time, Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party were in complete control.

links.title: A Cybrary of the Holocaust
links.description: An educational forum bringing together Holocaust survivors, children of Holocaust survivors, art by children, educational efforts, and Books by Survivors to promote learning and remembering.

links.title: Anne Frank Center
links.description: Educational materials about Anne Frank, the history of the Holocaust, and discrimination today.

links.title: The Holocaust Facts For Kids
links.description: The Holocaust was a terrible time when Nazi Germany and its helpers systematically murdered about six million Jewish people in Europe. This happened during World War II, between 1941 and 1945

450651.title: Pearl Harbor
450651.description: This category lists pages and sites about the bombing of Pearl Harbor. Japanese air forces launched a surprise attack on the U.S. military base during the morning hours of Dec. 7, 1941. The assault claimed the lives of 2,403 individuals, destroyed 188 planes, and damaged 8 battleships. In the hours that followed, the United States officially entered World War II.

links.title: Today in History: December  7
links.description: A brief history of the air raid, along with related photographs and documents. From the Library of Congress American Memory historic collections.

links.title: Attack At Pearl Harbor, 1941
links.description: Photographs and accounts from soldiers aboard the USS Arizona during the attack on Pearl Harbor. Includes some graphic descriptions.

links.title: Military Museum Loučka - Pearl Harbor
links.description: An overview of exhibited materials, exhibitions, acquired souvenirs, descendants of Czechoslovak soldiers who served in the US Army during the attack, and liturgical items of military chaplains.

450616.title: By Topic
450616.description: This category lists pages and sites that provide historical information focused on a specific topic.

450622.title: Age of Discovery
450622.description: This category lists pages and sites that provide information about the Age of Discovery, a period of time beginning in the 15th century in which people from many countries set out to find, explore, and settle new lands. The Age of Discovery overlapped the early years of the European Renaissance.

links.title: The Conquistadors
links.description: Online learning adventure retraces the footsteps of four Spanish explorers. From PBS.

links.title: Latitude: The Art and Science of Fifteenth-Century Navigation
links.description: A look at the tools, history, and knowledge 15th-century navigators had at their disposal as they set out in uncharted waters.

links.title: The Age Of Discovery
links.description: Shareware Hypercard stack designed to introduce young children to the era.

450617.title: Feudalism
450617.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about the feudal system, a political system similar to chiefdom that was in place in Europe, Japan and China for many centuries.

links.title: Feudalism
links.description: A brief introduction to feudal England.

links.title: YouTube: Japanese Feudalism
links.description: Watch the video of PowerPoint presentation, and listen the explanation about the feudalist system in Japan.

links.title: Feudal Japan: The Age of the Warrior
links.description: Learn about the samurai's job, and the western Influence.

links.title: Samurai Archives Japanese History Page
links.description: Very detailed and in-depth page dedicated to the research of Japanese Samurai history, with details of the warriors, battles, and culture.

links.title: Awesome Stories - Book Burning and Censorship
links.description: Tells the story of 1000 years of government censorship, with links to primary sources embedded in the text.

450618.title: Pirates
450618.description: This category is for sites about pirates and piracy. Piracy is robbery committed at sea. The main period of piracy occurred in the Caribbean Sea from the 1560s until the 1720s. However, piracy has happened before that time, and it still occurs today. It happens all over the world.    A pirate is someone who commits an act of piracy.

links.title: Pirates - Fact and Legend
links.description: Offers many facts on pirates in the 17th and 18th centuries.

links.title: Wikipedia: Piracy
links.description: An encyclopedia article about the history of piracy.

links.title: Pirates of the Bahamas
links.description: Offers a look at the history of pirates, focusing on Blackbeard, Anne Bonny, and Roger Vane.

links.title: Talk Like a Pirate Day
links.description: Background information and activities for those that want to be a pirate for a day.

links.title: Pirate's Cove
links.description: Includes pirate history and detailed biographies of pirates, privateers, and explorers.

links.title: Pirate Image Archive
links.description: Offers images of famous pirates, battles, and their ships.

links.title: Isle of Tortuga
links.description: Piracy at sea throughout history. Includes biographies and original documents.

links.title: Pirates of the Caribbean
links.description: A historical look at piracy in the Caribbean. Biographies of famous pirates, and guides to ships and weapons.

links.title: Legend of Blackbeard
links.description: Tells the story of Blackbeard the pirate.

links.title: Queen Anne's Revenge
links.description: Includes information about the archeology of the shipwreck of Blackbeard's flagship. View artifacts and read about conservation efforts.

450620.title: Wars and Warfare
450620.description: This category lists pages and sites that deal with wars and warfare.

links.title: Cold War Facts For Kids
links.description: The Cold War was a long period of tension and rivalry between the United States and its friends, and the Soviet Union (also known as the USSR) and its friends. It lasted from the end of World War II until the Soviet Union broke apart.

450763.title: Multimedia
450763.description: This category features audio and visual recordings of events in history.

links.title: American Memory from the Library of Congress
links.description: Offers materials relating to the history and culture of the United States. Includes topics such as history, geography, and economics.

links.title: Lost and Found Sound
links.description: National Public Radio series features sound recordings from famous people and ordinary people that capture the history of the late-19th and 20th centuries.

450764.title: Animated Battles
450764.description: Includes sites providing animated battles and explanatory texts about different wars and conflicts.

450767.title: Civil War
450767.description: Includes sites providing animated battles and explanatory texts about the Covol War in USA.

450765.title: Napoleonic Wars
450765.description: Includes sites providing animated battles and explanatory texts about the Napoleonic Wars.

links.title: BBC - History : Battle of Trafalgar
links.description: Animated map of the battle. Brief information.

links.title: The War Times Journal: Ia Drang and Landing Zone X-Ray
links.description: Animated map series showing the defense of the landing zone. Short history of the battle.

450766.title: WWI
450766.description: Includes sites providing animated battles and explanatory texts about the WW I.

links.title: BBC - The Western Front
links.description: The animation covers the front moving from 1914 to 1918 in Europe.

links.title: BBC - History :  Battle of the Somme
links.description: Includes animated map and explanatory notes.

450768.title: WWII
450768.description: Includes sites providing animated battles and explanatory texts about the WW II.

links.description: Provides information about commemorative events occurring during the centenary, both in Australia and overseas, as well as information and music to support a community-based commemorative event.

links.description: Includes animation of the battle and brief history.

links.description: Animated map and explanatory texts.

450653.title: This Day in History
450653.description: This category lists pages and sites that tell about significant events that occurred on a given day in history.

links.title: Born-on-this-Day.com
links.description: A searchable database of 80,000 famous people by day of birth, name, and fame. Also offers daily quotations, famous creative women section, and quote lookup.

links.title: This Date in Baseball History
links.description: Tells what happened in the world of baseball on a given date. Browse feature lets users see what happened on any day of the year.

links.title: The History of Today
links.description: Daily historical facts and events, famous birthdays, world and music history.

links.title: American Memory: Today in History
links.description: Each day an event from American history is illustrated by digitized items from the Library of Congress American Memory historic collections.

links.title: This Day in History on the History Channel
links.description: Highlights one major event in recent times, and provides a short list of past events. Also features special entries about this day in crime, entertainment, literary, war, technology, and automotive history.

450762.title: Timelines
450762.description: This category lists pages and sites that place historical people and events in a timeline sequence.

links.title: Science Timeline
links.description: A chronology from the 7th millenium BC to the present day, with brief explanations of events in the history of Western natural philosophy and sciences.

links.title: Strange Science: Timeline
links.description: Timeline of important events in paleontology and biology.

links.title: Food Timeline
links.description: Learn about the diets of prehistoric people, what the Vikings ate as they set off to explore the world, and how Thomas Jefferson made his ice cream.

links.title: Computer History Museum: A History of the Internet
links.description: Traces the phenomena from 1962 (before the term "Internet" was even coined) to the modern era.

links.title: Timeline of Art History
links.description: Provides an overview of the history of art as illustrated and represented in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

450781.title: Law
450781.description: This category lists pages and sites related to law, the rules of conduct and action laid down and enforced by government.

links.title: World Legal Information Institute
links.description: International directory of legal resources.

links.title: Law Library of Congress
links.description: The world's largest collection of law books and legal resources.

451138.title: Sociology
451138.description: Sociology involves the study of social relationships and institutions, including organizational behavior, societal development and structure, and cross-cultural interaction. The term "sociology" was coined in 1838 by Auguste Comte, but Max Weber and Émile Durkheim  are generally credited as the founders of the modern field.

links.title: Wikipedia: Sociology
links.description: Encyclopedia article covering the history of sociology as well as the scope of subjects and research methods.

links.title: Guide to College Majors in Sociology
links.description: Online education guide to find information on sociology career options and online degree programs.

links.title: Fact Monster - Sociology
links.description: Includes a short definition and an article on "The Evolution of Sociology".

451139.title: Sociologists
451139.description: This category includes sites about famous Sociologists. All sites are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment or for schoolwork. Biographies may be brief and sites may have several, perhaps connected by occupation, but the information contained should have the basic details, e.g., birth and death dates, some details of the life lived, major accomplishments, and so forth.

451146.title: Addams, Jane
451146.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Jane Addams (September 6, 1860 – May 21, 1935)in Cedarville, Illinois, Addams won the Nobel Peace Prize and was a founder of the U.S. Settlement House Movement.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Nobelprize.org - Jane Addams
links.description: Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1931. Includes biography, photograph and presentation speech.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Addams
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about her work and ideas.

links.title: Jane Addams Hull-House Museum
links.description: Short biography, detailed time line, exhibitions, collection, and education programmes.

links.title: Harvard University Library -  Jane Addams (1860-1935)
links.description: Biography for the activist, social worker, author, and Nobel Peace Prize winner, from the library's Open Collections Program.

links.title: Webster University - Jane Addams 1860-1935
links.description: Paper written by advanced seminar student Nicolle Bettis, with a focus on intellectual contributions and the unique impact and special problems that being female had on Addams’ career.

451143.title: Cooley, Charles
451143.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Charles Horton Cooley (1864-1929) an American sociologist born in Ann Arbor, Michigan.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Charles Cooley
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the American sociologist. Includes his works and a biography.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Cooley
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

451144.title: Martineau, Harriet
451144.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Harriet Martineau (June 12, 1802 - June 27, 1876) an English writer and philosopher, renowned in her day as a controversial journalist, political economist, abolitionist and life-long feminist.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Harriet Martineau
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the English writer and philosopher, known as a controversial journalist, political economist, abolitionist and life-long feminist.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index -  Martineau
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about her work and ideas.

links.title: Webster University - Harriet Martineau (1802 - 1876)
links.description: Paper written by an advanced seminar student with a focus on intellectual contributions and the unique impact and special problems that being female had on Martineau’s career.

451150.title: Marx, Karl
451150.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Karl Heinrich Marx (May 5, 1818 – March 14, 1883) a Prussian philosopher, political economist, and revolutionary. His work greatly influenced modern socialism, and he is considered one of the founders of economic history and sociology.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Karl Marx
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the Prussian philosopher, political economist, and revolutionary.

links.title: Fact Monster - Karl Marx
links.description: Short biography for the founder of modern communism. Includes links to related articles.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Marx
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

links.title: Karl Marx Facts For Kids
links.description: Karl Marx (born May 5, 1818 – died March 14, 1883) was a very important German thinker. He was a philosopher (someone who studies big ideas), an economist (someone who studies money and how societies work), a historian (someone who studies the past), and a journalist.

451142.title: Mead, George Herbert
451142.description:
This category lists pages and sites about George Herbert Mead (February 27, 1863 – April 26, 1931) an American philosopher, sociologist and psychologist, primarily affiliated with the University of Chicago, where he was one of several distinguished pragmatists. He is regarded as one of the founders of social psychology.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - George Herbert Mead
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the American philosopher, sociologist and psychologist. Provides a biography and information on his work.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Mead
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

451149.title: Pareto, Vilfredo
451149.description:
This category lists pages and sites about the French-Italian sociologist, economist and philosopher Vilfredo Pareto (July 15, 1848, Paris – August 19, 1923, Geneva) He made several important contributions especially in the study of income distribution and in the analysis of individuals' choices.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork.

links.title: Mind and Society by Vilfredo Pareto
links.description: First few pages of Pareto's opus magnum on economic theory.

451140.title: Park, Robert E.
451140.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Robert Ezra Park (February 14, 1864–February 7, 1944) an American urban sociologist, one of the main founders of the original Chicago School of sociology.

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Robert E. Park
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the  American urban sociologist, one of the main founders of the original Chicago School of sociology.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Park
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

451147.title: Simmel, Georg
451147.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Georg Simmel (March 1, 1858 – September 28, 1918). Born in Berlin, Germany Simmel was one of the first generation of German sociologists. His most famous works today are "The Philosophy of Money", "The Stranger" and "The Metropolis and Mental Life".

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Georg Simmel
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the German sociologist. Includes a list of his works as an   essayist and author of sociological and philosophical books.

links.title: Georg Simmel: Biographic Information
links.description: Biography and career information provided by Prof. Dr. Hans Geser of Universität Zürich.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Simmel
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

451148.title: Spencer, Herbert
451148.description:
This category lists pages and sites about Herbert Spencer (27 April 1820 – 8 December 1903), an English philosopher and prominent classic-liberal political theorist. He is now best known for his political theories related to what has become known as Social Darwinism and for coining the term survival of the fittest

All sites listed here are suitable for children and teens to read and use for enjoyment and/or for schoolwork. Please suggest only sites appropriate for children under the age of 18.

links.title: Wikipedia - Herbert Spencer
links.description: Encyclopedia article about the English philosopher and prominent classic-liberal political theorist.

links.title: Victorian Web: Herbert Spencer (1820-1903)
links.description: Contains biographical materials and articles related to his views on politics, society and science.

links.title: Dead Sociologists Index - Spencer
links.description: Biographical introduction with articles about his work and ideas.

links.title: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Herbert Spencer
links.description: In depth biographical article about the British philosopher and sociologist. Written by William Sweet.

451145.title: Veblen, Thorstein
451145.description:

445166.title: Letterboxing
445166.description: Letterboxing is a outdoor recreational activity which combines collecting, puzzle-solving, and treasure hunting.  Briefly, letterboxing enthusiasts hide and hunt weatherproof containers in remote or scenic places. Each container holds a guestbook, a rubber stamp and stamp pad. The planter of the letterbox distributes clues to its location; solution of these clues may require a combination of skills such as mapreading, orienteering, and puzzle-solving.  Letterboxers carry their own stamp book and personal stamp when hunting for hidden boxes. Upon finding a letterbox, they will impress their own book using the found stamp, and leave their own stamping or personalization in the letterbox guestbook.  Letterboxing has its roots in Dartmoor, England, in 1854.

445238.title: Rugby League
445238.description: This category lists Rugby Football League sites that kids ages 3-18 can use to learn about the sport.   In 1895, when 12 clubs decided to split from the Northern Rugby Football Union, few could have envisaged that 100 years later, the game of rugby league would become the second most popular spectator sport in Britain and spread as far and wide as Australia, New Zealand and even Papua New Guinea.  Two teams take part in a game of rugby league with 13 players on each team at "kick off". Each team also have 4 substitutes/replacements available to bring on at any appropriate moment in the game. Each teams "13" is made up of 7 "backs" and 6 "forwards" . The backs are generally regarded as the attacking players and usually have more pace than the bigger more powerful forwards who are usually the "yard" makers.   The object of the game is for one team to score more points than the other team. There are 80 minutes in which to do this. A team can score points through scoring a "try" or kicking a "goal".

445253.description: This category lists sites that kids ages 3-18 can use to learn about futsal.  The term "futsal" comes from "futbol de salon" or "indoor soccer." Futsal is a five-a-side version of soccer played indoors on a basketball-sized court (no walls). Futsal has experienced tremendous growth and is the only indoor version of soccer with a sanctioned world championship. The sport is played internationally, with recognized continental and club championships. Futsal is the only "official form of Indoor Soccer" as approved by (FIFA) Federation Internationale de Football Association. It is played in all the continents of the world by over 100 countries and has 12 million players.

446954.title: Young Caregivers
446954.description: A young carer is under 18 years of age. They help look after a parent, brother, sister or another relative or friend who due to their disability, frailty, illness or vulnerability cannot care for themselves without help. Young carers face serious caring responsibilities. In addition to the daily tasks they complete for their parents such as housework, cooking and bathing, they live with the added pressure of school and, often, a lack of understanding from schoolmates.
